source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Existing public labels match Hebrew 8–20, retaining 8:23 and 9:1–25. Common English labels 9:1–26 differ; no relabeling performed. Jeremiah 10:11 is Aramaic.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains all five groups and repeated bones; reads recorded plural verb without identifying the agents.
verses.before: At that time, declares the LORD, they will bring out from their graves the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of its officials, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.after: “At that time,” declares the **LORD**, “the bones of Judah’s kings and officials, the bones of the priests and prophets, and the bones of Jerusalem’s inhabitants will be brought out of their graves.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time, declares the LORD, they will bring out from their graves the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of its officials, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps the five worship verbs and shame of unburied remains before the objects of devotion.
verses.before: They will spread them before the sun and the moon and all the host of the heavens, which they loved, served, followed, sought, and bowed down to. They will not be gathered or buried; they will become dung on the face of the ground.
verses.after: They will be spread out before the sun, the moon, and all the host of heaven—the ones they loved, served, followed, sought, and bowed down to. The bones will not be gathered or buried. They will lie like dung on the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will spread them before the sun and the moon and all the host of the heavens, which they loved, served, followed, sought, and bowed down to. They will not be gathered or buried; they will become dung on the face of the ground.

verses.rationale: Preserves exile and survivors without smoothing the stated preference for death.
verses.before: Death will be chosen rather than life by all the remnant who remain of this evil family, in every place where I have driven them, declares the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: All who remain of this evil family will prefer death to life, wherever I have driven the survivors,” declares the **LORD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Death will be chosen rather than life by all the remnant who remain of this evil family, in every place where I have driven them, declares the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Makes generic subjects clear while retaining paired questions and turn wordplay.
verses.before: You will say to them: Thus says the LORD: Do people fall and not rise again? Do they turn away and not return?
verses.after: “Tell them: This is what the **LORD** says: When people fall, don’t they get up? When someone turns away, doesn’t that person turn back?
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall say to them: Thus says the LORD: Do people fall and not rise again? Do they turn away and not return?

verses.rationale: Keeps Jerusalem’s apposition and repeated return language.
verses.before: Why has this people, Jerusalem, turned away in a lasting turning away? They hold fast to deceit; they refuse to return.
verses.after: Then why has this people turned away— Jerusalem—in a lasting refusal to return? They cling to deceit; they refuse to turn back.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why has this people, Jerusalem, turned away in a lasting turning away? They hold fast to deceit; they refuse to return.

verses.rationale: Follows recorded course reading and retains self-question and battle image.
verses.before: I have listened and heard: they do not speak what is right. No one repents of their evil, saying, “What have I done?” All of them turn to their own course, like a horse rushing into battle.
verses.after: I have listened closely, but they do not speak honestly. No one regrets their evil and asks, ‘What have I done?’ Everyone returns to their own course, like a horse charging into battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have listened and heard: they do not speak what is right. No one repents of their evil, saying, “What have I done?” All of them turn to their own course, like a horse rushing into battle.

verses.rationale: Retains four birds, recorded swift reading, and contrast with divine judgment.
verses.before: Even the stork in the heavens knows its appointed times; the dove, the swift, and the crane keep the time of their coming. But my people do not know the judgment of the LORD.
verses.after: Even the stork in the sky knows its appointed seasons; the turtledove, swift, and crane keep the time of their return. But my people do not know the **LORD**’s judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even the stork in the heavens knows its appointed times; the dove, the swift, and the crane keep the time of their coming. But my people do not know the judgment of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps challenge to scribal handling of instruction; does not expand into a theory of scripture.
verses.before: How can you say, “We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us”? Look, certainly, the lying pen of the scribes has made it a lie.
verses.after: How can you say, ‘We are wise; the **LORD**’s instruction is with us’? Look—the lying pen of the scribes has turned it into a lie.
verses.tsw_comparator: How can you say, “We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us”? Look, certainly, the lying pen of the scribes has made it a lie.

verses.rationale: Preserves rejection as basis of the rhetorical wisdom question.
verses.before: The wise are put to shame; they are dismayed and caught. Look, they have rejected the word of the LORD; what wisdom do they have?
verses.after: The wise are put to shame, shattered and trapped. They have rejected the **LORD**’s word; what wisdom do they have?
verses.tsw_comparator: The wise are put to shame; they are dismayed and caught. Look, they have rejected the word of the LORD; what wisdom do they have?

verses.rationale: Retains gender-specific threatened dispossession and both social ranges.
verses.before: So I will give their wives to others, their fields to people who will possess them. For from the least to the greatest, every one of them is greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, every one of them deals falsely.
verses.after: So I will give their wives to others and their fields to new owners. From the least to the greatest, everyone is greedy for gain. From prophet to priest, everyone deals in lies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I will give their wives to others, their fields to those who will possess them. For from the least to the greatest, every one of them is greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, every one of them deals falsely.

verses.rationale: Retains personified daughter and repeated peace rather than flattening to reassurance.
verses.before: They have treated the wound of the daughter of my people lightly, saying, “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace.
verses.after: They treat the wound of my daughter, my people, as though it were slight, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have treated the wound of the daughter of my people lightly, saying, “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace.

verses.rationale: Keeps shame questions and fall/stumble imagery; renders visitation as accountability.
verses.before: Were they ashamed because they did an abomination? No, they were not ashamed at all; they did not know how to blush. Therefore they will fall among people who fall; at the time of their punishment they will stumble, says the LORD.
verses.after: Were they ashamed of the detestable things they did? They felt no shame at all; they did not know how to blush. So they will fall among the fallen; when I call them to account, they will stumble,” says the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Were they ashamed because they did an abomination? No, they were not ashamed at all; they did not know how to blush. Therefore they will fall among those who fall; at the time of their punishment they will stumble, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Adopts removal sense in difficult gathering verb and states uncertainty about last clause in note.
verses.before: I will surely gather them, declares the LORD. There are no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree, and the leaf has withered; and I have given them things that will pass over them.
verses.after: “I will sweep them away,” declares the **LORD**. “No grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree; the leaves have withered. What I gave them will pass away from them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will surely gather them, declares the LORD. There are no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree, and the leaf has withered; and I have given them things that will pass over them.

verses.rationale: Retains collective speech, repeated divine names, and destruction sense of silence verb.
verses.before: Why are we sitting still? Gather yourselves, and let us go into the fortified cities and perish there, for the LORD our God has brought us to ruin and given us poisonous water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.
verses.after: “Why are we sitting here? Gather together! Let’s enter the fortified cities and perish there. For the **LORD** our God has doomed us and given us poisoned water to drink, because we sinned against the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why are we sitting still? Gather yourselves, and let us go into the fortified cities and perish there, for the LORD our God has brought us to ruin and given us poisonous water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps peace/healing hopes and abrupt terror.
verses.before: We hoped for peace, but there was no good; for a time of healing, but look—terror!
verses.after: We hoped for peace, but no good came; for a time of healing, but look—terror!”
verses.tsw_comparator: We hoped for peace, but there was no good; for a time of healing, but look—terror!

verses.rationale: Leaves unnamed enemy possessive intact; preserves Dan and total devastation.
verses.before: From Dan is heard the snorting of his horses; at the sound of the neighing of his stallions, the whole land shakes. They come and devour the land and all that fills it, the city and people who live in it.
verses.after: From Dan comes the snorting of his horses; at the neighing of his stallions, the whole land trembles. They come and devour the land and all it holds, the city and those who live in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Dan is heard the snorting of his horses; at the sound of the neighing of his stallions, the whole land shakes. They come and devour the land and all that fills it, the city and those who live in it.

verses.rationale: Keeps serpent attack as divine speech, without turning it into an explicit allegory.
verses.before: For look, I am sending among you snakes, vipers that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you, declares the LORD.
verses.after: “Look, I am sending snakes among you, adders that cannot be charmed. They will bite you,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, I am sending among you snakes, vipers that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you, declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Uses tentative comfort sense of rare expression; note marks uncertainty and speaker ambiguity.
verses.before: My comfort in grief! My heart is faint within me.
verses.after: My comfort fails in sorrow; my heart is sick within me.
verses.tsw_comparator: My comfort in grief! My heart is faint within me.

verses.rationale: Keeps voices distinct through quotation and preserves idols as empty things.
verses.before: Look—the cry of the daughter of my people from a distant land: “Is the LORD not in Zion? Is her king not in her?” “Why have they provoked me to anger with their carved images, with foreign vanities?”
verses.after: Listen! My daughter, my people, cries out from a distant land: ‘Is the **LORD** no longer in Zion? Is her king no longer there?’ ‘Why have they provoked me with their carved images, with foreign things of emptiness?’
verses.tsw_comparator: Look—the cry of the daughter of my people from a distant land: “Is the LORD not in Zion? Is her king not in her?” “Why have they provoked me to anger with their carved images, with foreign vanities?”

verses.rationale: Preserves compact seasonal lament without interpreting rescue timing.
verses.before: “The harvest has passed, the summer has ended, and we have not been saved.”
verses.after: “The harvest is past, the summer is over, and we have not been saved.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “The harvest has passed, the summer has ended, and we have not been saved.”

verses.rationale: Preserves shared breaking language and mourning voice.
verses.before: For the wound of the daughter of my people I am shattered; I mourn; horror has seized me.
verses.after: At the breaking of my daughter, my people, I am broken. I mourn; horror has taken hold of me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the wound of the daughter of my people I am shattered; I mourn; horror has seized me.

verses.rationale: Retains three questions and regional healing image rather than answering them.
verses.before: Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why then has the healing of the daughter of my people not come?
verses.after: Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no healer there? Why, then, has healing not come to my daughter, my people?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why then has the healing of the daughter of my people not come?

verses.rationale: Retains repository Hebrew 8:23 label and embodied unending lament; common English numbering places this at 9:1.
verses.before: Oh, that my head were water, and my eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people.
verses.after: If only my head were water and my eyes a spring of tears! I would weep day and night for the slain of my daughter, my people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Oh, that my head were water, and my eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people.

verses.rationale: Retains repository Hebrew 9:1 label and desire to leave the adulterous gathering; common English numbering places this at 9:2.
verses.before: Who will give me a travelers’ lodge in the wilderness, that I may leave my people and go away from them? For they are all adulterers, a band of traitors.
verses.after: If only I had a travelers’ shelter in the wilderness! I would leave my people and go away from them. For they are all adulterers, a gathering of traitors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who will give me a travelers’ lodge in the wilderness, that I may leave my people and go away from them? For they are all adulterers, a band of traitors.

verses.rationale: Keeps tongue-bow image and failure to know God without identifying a human speaker.
verses.before: They bend their tongue, their bow, for falsehood; they are not strong in the land for faithfulness. For they go out from evil to evil, and they do not know me, declares the LORD.
verses.after: “They bend their tongues like bows; lies, not faithfulness, prevail in the land. They go from one evil to another and do not know me,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: They bend their tongue, their bow, for falsehood; they are not strong in the land for faithfulness. For they go out from evil to evil, and they do not know me, declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains brother alongside neighbor and notes Jacob-like verbal wordplay.
verses.before: Let each guard against a neighbor, and trust no brother; for every brother surely supplants, and every neighbor goes about as a slanderer.
verses.after: “Beware of your neighbor; do not trust any brother. Every brother is a schemer, and every neighbor spreads slander.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let each guard against a neighbor, and trust no brother; for every brother surely supplants, and every neighbor goes about as a slanderer.

verses.rationale: Keeps learned lying and exhausting wrongdoing rather than moral paraphrase.
verses.before: Each deceives a neighbor, and they do not speak truth. They have taught their tongues to speak falsehood; they weary themselves doing wrong.
verses.after: They deceive one another and do not speak the truth. They have trained their tongues to lie; they wear themselves out doing wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: Each deceives a neighbor, and they do not speak truth. They have taught their tongues to speak falsehood; they weary themselves doing wrong.

verses.rationale: Retains singular you and plural their without forced speaker identification.
verses.before: Your dwelling is among deceit; through deceit they refuse to know me, declares the LORD.
verses.after: You live surrounded by deceit. In their deceit they refuse to know me,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit; through deceit they refuse to know me, declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps refining/testing and difficult motivating question.
verses.before: So, thus says the LORD of Hosts: Look, I am refining them and testing them; for what else can I do because of my people’s daughter?
verses.after: So this is what the **LORD** of hosts says: “Look, I will refine them and test them. What else can I do because of my daughter, my people?
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, thus says the LORD of Hosts: Look, I am refining them and testing them; for what else can I do because of my people’s daughter?

verses.rationale: Uses deadly sense of arrow adjective with written/read uncertainty noted.
verses.before: Their tongue is a slaughtering arrow; it speaks deceit. With his mouth one speaks peace to a neighbor, but within himself he sets an ambush.
verses.after: Their tongue is a deadly arrow; it speaks deceit. With the mouth, someone speaks peace to a neighbor, while inwardly laying an ambush.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their tongue is a slaughtering arrow; it speaks deceit. With his mouth one speaks peace to a neighbor, but within himself he sets an ambush.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated judgment questions and personal divine vengeance.
verses.before: Will I not punish them for these things? declares the LORD. Will I not take vengeance on a nation like this?
verses.after: Should I not call them to account for this?” declares the **LORD**. “Should I not avenge myself on a nation like this?
verses.tsw_comparator: Shall I not punish them for these things? declares the LORD. Shall I not take vengeance on a nation like this?

verses.rationale: Preserves first-person lament and animal loss, without overassigning speaker.
verses.before: For the mountains I will lift up weeping and lamentation, and for the wilderness pastures, a dirge. For they are burned up, with no one passing through; they do not hear the sound of livestock. From birds of the sky to animals, they have fled; they have gone away.
verses.after: I will lift up weeping and wailing over the mountains, a lament over the wilderness pastures. They are burned out; no one passes through. No sound of livestock is heard. Birds of the sky and animals alike have fled and gone.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the mountains I will lift up weeping and lamentation, and for the wilderness pastures, a dirge. For they are burned up, with no one passing through; they do not hear the sound of livestock. From birds of the sky to animals, they have fled; they have gone away.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine devastation and concrete jackal habitation.
verses.before: I will make Jerusalem a heap of ruins, a lair of jackals; and I will make the towns of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.
verses.after: I will make Jerusalem a heap of ruins, a home for jackals. I will make Judah’s cities desolate, with no one living there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make Jerusalem a heap of ruins, a lair of jackals; and I will make the towns of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.

verses.rationale: Keeps three linked questions and asks for an explanation rather than supplying one early.
verses.before: Who is wise enough to understand this? To whom has the mouth of the LORD spoken, that they may declare it? Why has the land perished, burned up like the wilderness, with no one passing through?
verses.after: Who is wise enough to understand this? To whom has the **LORD** spoken, so that they can explain it? Why has the land perished, burned out like a wilderness where no one passes?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is wise enough to understand this? To whom has the mouth of the LORD spoken, that they may declare it? Why has the land perished, burned up like the wilderness, with no one passing through?

verses.rationale: Keeps instruction, hearing, and walking as linked covenant images.
verses.before: And the LORD said: Because they have abandoned my instruction, which I set before them, and have not listened to my voice or walked in it.
verses.after: The **LORD** said, “Because they abandoned my instruction, which I set before them. They did not listen to my voice or walk in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said: Because they have abandoned my instruction, which I set before them, and have not listened to my voice or walked in it.

verses.rationale: Preserves fathers as transmitters and plural Baals.
verses.before: Instead, they have followed the stubbornness of their heart and the Baals, as their ancestors taught them.
verses.after: Instead, they followed their stubborn hearts and the Baals, as their fathers taught them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Instead, they have followed the stubbornness of their heart and the Baals, as their ancestors taught them.

verses.rationale: Retains food and drink judgment images without substituting abstract suffering.
verses.before: So, thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I will feed this people wormwood, and I will give them poisonous water to drink.
verses.after: So this is what the **LORD** of hosts, Israel’s God, says: “Look, I am feeding this people wormwood and giving them poisoned water to drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I will feed this people wormwood, and I will give them poisonous water to drink.

verses.rationale: Retains unfamiliar exile destinations and full force of threatened destruction.
verses.before: I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their ancestors have known. I will send the sword after them until I have destroyed them.
verses.after: I will scatter them among nations neither they nor their fathers knew. I will send the sword after them until I have brought them to an end.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their ancestors have known. I will send the sword after them until I have destroyed them.

verses.rationale: Keeps female specialists and repeated summons.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Consider, and call for the mourning women, that they may come; send for the skilled women, that they may come.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** of hosts says: “Consider this: call the mourning women; let them come. Send for the skilled women; let them come.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Consider, and call for the mourning women, that they may come; send for the skilled women, that they may come.

verses.rationale: Preserves plural us and embodied mourning without correcting speaker shift.
verses.before: Let them hurry and raise a lament over us, that tears may run down from our eyes and water flow from our eyelids.
verses.after: Let them hurry and lift up a wail over us, so our eyes stream with tears and our eyelids flow with water.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them hurry and raise a lament over us, that tears may run down from our eyes and water flow from our eyelids.

verses.rationale: Chooses destruction sense for difficult dwelling clause; note retains displacement alternative.
verses.before: For the sound of lamentation is heard from Zion: “How we are devastated! We are deeply ashamed, for we have left the land, because they have cast down our dwellings.”
verses.after: For a voice of wailing is heard from Zion: ‘How we have been devastated! How deeply we are ashamed! We have left the land; our homes have been torn down.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For the sound of lamentation is heard from Zion: “How we are devastated! We are deeply ashamed, for we have left the land, because they have cast down our dwellings.”

verses.rationale: Keeps female address and transmission of lament across generations.
verses.before: For hear, women, the word of the LORD; let your ear receive the word of his mouth. Teach your daughters a lament, and each woman her companion a dirge.
verses.after: Women, hear the **LORD**’s word; let your ears receive what his mouth says. Teach your daughters to wail, and one another to lament.
verses.tsw_comparator: For hear, women, the word of the LORD; let your ear receive the word of his mouth. Teach your daughters a lament, and each woman her companion a dirge.

verses.rationale: Retains personified intruding Death and age/gender-specific victims.
verses.before: For death has come up through our windows; it has entered our fortresses, to cut off children from the streets and young men from the squares.
verses.after: Death has climbed through our windows and entered our palaces, to cut off children from the street and young men from the squares.
verses.tsw_comparator: For death has come up through our windows; it has entered our fortresses, to cut off children from the streets and young men from the squares.

verses.rationale: Retains unburied corpses and agricultural image without euphemism.
verses.before: Speak: Thus declares the LORD: “The corpse of humanity will fall like dung on the open field, like sheaves behind the reaper, with no one to gather them.”
verses.after: Say: ‘This is what the **LORD** declares: Human corpses will fall like dung on the open field, like cut grain behind the reaper, with no one to gather it.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Speak: Thus declares the LORD: “The corpse of humanity will fall like dung on the open field, like sheaves behind the reaper, with no one to gather them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps three parallel prohibitions and root repetitions.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Let not the wise boast in their wisdom; let not the mighty boast in their strength; let not the rich boast in their wealth.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “Let the wise not boast in their wisdom, the strong not boast in their strength, or the rich boast in their riches.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Let not the wise boast in their wisdom; let not the mighty boast in their strength; let not the rich boast in their wealth.

verses.rationale: Retains knowing God and three consequential biblical terms; both names retained.
verses.before: But let the one who boasts boast in this: that they understand and know me, that I am the LORD, who practices steadfast love, justice, and righteousness in the land; for in these things I delight, declares the LORD.
verses.after: Let anyone who boasts boast in this: that they understand and know me, that I am the **LORD**, who acts with steadfast love, justice, and righteousness on earth. For these are what delight me,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: But let the one who boasts boast in this: that they understand and know me, that I am the LORD, who practices steadfast love, justice, and righteousness in the land; for in these things I delight, declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves deliberately paradoxical circumcision language and continuing list.
verses.before: Look, days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish everyone circumcised in uncircumcision:
verses.after: “Look, days are coming,” declares the **LORD**, “when I will call to account all who are circumcised yet uncircumcised—
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish everyone circumcised in uncircumcision:

verses.rationale: Retains Judah in list, hair practice, and bodily/heart contrast without harmonization.
verses.before: Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all people who clip the edge of their hair, who live in the wilderness. For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.
verses.after: Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all who clip the edges of their hair and live in the wilderness. For all these nations are uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all those who clip the edge of their hair, who live in the wilderness. For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.

verses.rationale: Keeps collective Israel address and divine speech.
verses.before: Hear the word that the LORD has spoken concerning you, house of Israel.
verses.after: House of Israel, hear the word the **LORD** has spoken about you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear the word that the LORD has spoken concerning you, house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains signs and nations contrast without importing astrology details into text.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be dismayed by the signs of the heavens, though the nations are dismayed by them.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “Do not learn the way of the nations or be terrified by signs in the sky, though the nations are terrified by them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be dismayed by the signs of the heavens, though the nations are dismayed by them.

verses.rationale: Keeps emptiness image and human manufacture; tool identification remains broad.
verses.before: For the customs of the peoples are emptiness: a tree is cut from the forest, the work of a craftsperson’s hands with an axe.
verses.after: The peoples’ customs are emptiness. Someone cuts a tree from the forest; a craftworker shapes it with a tool.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the customs of the peoples are emptiness: a tree is cut from the forest, the work of a craftsperson’s hands with an axe.

verses.rationale: Preserves material sequence and dependence on fastening.
verses.before: They adorn it with silver and gold; they fasten it with nails and hammers so that it will not topple.
verses.after: They adorn it with silver and gold, fasten it with nails and hammers so it will not wobble.
verses.tsw_comparator: They adorn it with silver and gold; they fasten it with nails and hammers so that it will not topple.

verses.rationale: Uses field-scarecrow reading with alternative noted; retains both limits of agency.
verses.before: Like a scarecrow in a cucumber field, they cannot speak; they must be carried, for they cannot walk. Do not fear them, for they cannot do harm, nor is it in them to do good.
verses.after: Like scarecrows in a cucumber field, they cannot speak. They must be carried, because they cannot walk. Do not fear them: they can do no harm, and they have no power to do good.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a scarecrow in a cucumber field, they cannot speak; they must be carried, for they cannot walk. Do not fear them, for they cannot do harm, nor is it in them to do good.

verses.rationale: Preserves direct prayer and repeated greatness.
verses.before: There is none like you, LORD; you are great, and your name is great in might.
verses.after: No one is like you, **LORD**. You are great; your name is great in might.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is none like you, LORD; you are great, and your name is great in might.

verses.rationale: Keeps universal kingship and fear due to God without changing it to admiration.
verses.before: Who would not fear you, King of the nations? For this is your due. For among all the wise of the nations and in all their kingdoms, there is none like you.
verses.after: Who would not fear you, King of the nations? It is your due. Among all the nations’ wise ones and throughout their kingdoms, no one is like you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who would not fear you, King of the nations? For this is your due. For among all the wise of the nations and in all their kingdoms, there is none like you.

verses.rationale: Keeps sharp equation of idol instruction with wood; note acknowledges compressed syntax.
verses.before: Together they are dull and foolish; the instruction of idols is wood.
verses.after: All together they are senseless and foolish; the instruction of empty idols is only wood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Together they are dull and foolish; the instruction of idols is wood.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned Uphaz, trade materials, colors, and workmanship.
verses.before: Hammered silver is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz— the work of a craftsperson and of a goldsmith’s hands. Blue and purple are their clothing; all of them are the work of skilled artisans.
verses.after: Beaten silver comes from Tarshish and gold from Uphaz, the work of a craftworker and a goldsmith’s hands. Blue and purple are their clothing; all of it is skilled workers’ handiwork.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hammered silver is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz— the work of a craftsperson and of a goldsmith’s hands. Blue and purple are their clothing; all of them are the work of skilled artisans.

verses.rationale: Retains contrast and distinct divine titles.
verses.before: But the LORD is the true God; he is the living God and the everlasting King. At his wrath the earth quakes, and the nations cannot endure his indignation.
verses.after: But the **LORD** is the true God; he is the living God and everlasting King. The earth trembles at his anger; the nations cannot endure his fury.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD is the true God; he is the living God and the everlasting King. At his wrath the earth quakes, and the nations cannot endure his indignation.

verses.rationale: Translates the Aramaic sentence directly; preserves make/vanish wordplay in note rather than invented rhyme.
verses.before: Thus you will say to them: “The gods that did not make the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth and from beneath these heavens.”
verses.after: This is what you are to tell them: “The gods who did not make the heavens and the earth will vanish from the earth and from beneath these heavens.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus you shall say to them: “The gods that did not make the heavens and the earth shall perish from the earth and from beneath these heavens.”

verses.rationale: Keeps three creation actions and corresponding attributes.
verses.before: He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
verses.after: He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.

verses.rationale: Keeps heavenly water and storehouse imagery; reads recorded definite earth.
verses.before: When he gives his voice, there is a roar of waters in the heavens; he causes clouds to rise from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
verses.after: When he gives voice, waters roar in the heavens. He raises clouds from the ends of the earth, makes lightning for the rain, and brings wind out of his storehouses.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he gives his voice, there is a roar of waters in the heavens; he causes clouds to rise from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses.

verses.rationale: Keeps universal human limitation, craftworker shame, and absent breath.
verses.before: Every person is dull, without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by an idol. For the image he has cast is a lie, and there is no breath in them.
verses.after: Everyone is senseless, without knowledge; every goldsmith is shamed by the carved image. The image he casts is a lie; there is no breath in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every person is dull, without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by an idol. For the image he has cast is a lie, and there is no breath in them.

verses.rationale: Preserves emptiness and visitation language without giving idols actual divinity.
verses.before: They are emptiness, a work of mockery; at the time of their punishment, they will perish.
verses.after: They are emptiness, objects of mockery. When they are called to account, they will perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are emptiness, a work of mockery; at the time of their punishment, they will perish.

verses.rationale: Retains mutual portion/inheritance relationship and divine title.
verses.before: The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for he is the Maker of everything, and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance; the LORD of Hosts is his name.
verses.after: Jacob’s portion is not like these, for he is the one who forms everything. Israel is the tribe of his inheritance; the **LORD** of hosts is his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for he is the Maker of all things, and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance; the LORD of Hosts is his name.

verses.rationale: Follows recorded feminine resident and retains urgent packing image.
verses.before: Gather up your bundle from the land, you who live under siege.
verses.after: Gather your bundle from the ground, you who live under siege.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gather up your bundle from the land, you who live under siege.

verses.rationale: Retains sling metaphor and difficult find clause with note rather than unsupported detailed outcome.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: Look, I am slinging out the inhabitants of the land at this time, and I will bring distress upon them, so that they may find it.
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** says: “This time I am slinging out the land’s inhabitants. I will press them hard, so that they feel it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: Look, I am slinging out the inhabitants of the land at this time, and I will bring distress upon them, so that they may find it.

verses.rationale: Keeps lament and self-address; does not force identification of personified speaker.
verses.before: Woe is me because of my brokenness! My wound is grievous. Yet I said, “Surely this is my sickness, and I must bear it.”
verses.after: Oh, my brokenness! My wound is severe. Yet I said, “This is my sickness, and I must bear it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe is me because of my brokenness! My wound is grievous. But I said, “Surely this is my sickness, and I must bear it.”

verses.rationale: Retains tent family image and ambiguous absence/death of children.
verses.before: My tent has been ravaged, and all my cords have been torn away. My children have gone from me, and they are no more; there is no one left to spread my tent again or to set up my tent curtains.
verses.after: My tent is destroyed; all its ropes are snapped. My children have gone from me and are no more. There is no one left to pitch my tent or hang its curtains.
verses.tsw_comparator: My tent has been ravaged, and all my cords have been torn away. My children have gone from me, and they are no more; there is no one left to spread my tent again or to set up my tent curtains.

verses.rationale: Keeps shepherd metaphor and causal failure without naming a modern institution.
verses.before: For the shepherds have become dull and have not sought the LORD; so they have not acted wisely, and all their flock has been scattered.
verses.after: The shepherds have become senseless and have not sought the **LORD**. So they have not prospered, and their whole flock is scattered.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the shepherds have become dull and have not sought the LORD; therefore they have not acted wisely, and all their flock has been scattered.

verses.rationale: Preserves unnamed northern threat and repeated jackal image.
verses.before: The sound of a report—look, it is coming! A great shaking from the land of the north, to make the cities of Judah a desolation, a dwelling place of jackals.
verses.after: Listen—a report is coming! A great uproar from the northern land, to turn Judah’s cities into a wasteland, a home for jackals.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sound of a report—look, it is coming! A great shaking from the land of the north, to make the cities of Judah a desolation, a dwelling place of jackals.

verses.rationale: Keeps road/steps image and generic human scope.
verses.before: I know, LORD, that a person’s way is not their own; it is not for one who walks to direct their steps.
verses.after: I know, **LORD**, that people do not own their way; those who walk cannot direct their own steps.
verses.tsw_comparator: I know, LORD, that a person’s way is not their own; it is not for one who walks to direct their steps.

verses.rationale: Retains request for correction and justice rather than immunity.
verses.before: Correct me, LORD, but with justice; not in your anger, lest you make me few.
verses.after: Correct me, **LORD**, but with justice, not in your anger, or you will reduce me to nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: Correct me, LORD, but with justice; not in your anger, lest you make me few.

verses.rationale: Preserves harsh prayer and repeated devouring rather than toning down vengeance.
verses.before: Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you, and on the families that do not call on your name. For they have devoured Jacob; they have devoured him and brought him to an end, and they have made his dwelling place desolate.
verses.after: Pour out your fury on the nations that do not know you, on the families that do not call on your name. For they have devoured Jacob— devoured him and consumed him— and laid waste his home.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you, and on the families that do not call on your name. For they have devoured Jacob; they have devoured him and brought him to an end, and they have made his dwelling place desolate.

verses.rationale: Retains prophetic introduction without adding a historical date.
verses.before: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying:
verses.after: The word that came to Jeremiah from the **LORD**:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying:

verses.rationale: Keeps plural hear and singular commission in English without inventing the audience’s identity.
verses.before: “Hear the words of this covenant, and speak them to the people of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.after: “Hear the words of this covenant, and speak them to the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Hear the words of this covenant, and speak them to the people of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserves covenant curse and continuing sentence.
verses.before: Say to them, ‘Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Cursed is the one who does not hear the words of this covenant,
verses.after: Tell them: This is what the **LORD**, Israel’s God, says: Cursed is anyone who does not listen to the words of this covenant,
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to them, ‘Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Cursed is the one who does not hear the words of this covenant,

verses.rationale: Retains iron furnace and reciprocal covenant formula.
verses.before: which I commanded your ancestors on the day I brought them out from the land of Egypt, from the iron furnace, saying: “Hear my voice, and do them, according to all that I command you. Then you will be my people, and I will be your God,
verses.after: which I commanded your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, out of the iron furnace. I said, ‘Listen to my voice and do everything I command you. Then you will be my people, and I will be your God.’
verses.tsw_comparator: which I commanded your ancestors on the day I brought them out from the land of Egypt, from the iron furnace, saying: “Hear my voice, and do them, according to all that I command you. Then you will be my people, and I will be your God,

verses.rationale: Keeps oath, inherited land image, and prophet’s audible response.
verses.before: that I may establish the oath that I swore to your ancestors, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day.”’” I answered and said, “Amen, O LORD.”
verses.after: This was to fulfill the oath I swore to your ancestors, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is today.” I answered, “Amen, **LORD**.”
verses.tsw_comparator: that I may establish the oath that I swore to your ancestors, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day.”’” And I answered and said, “Amen, O LORD.”

verses.rationale: Retains public locations and hearing-to-doing link.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to me, “Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, saying: ‘Hear the words of this covenant and do them.
verses.after: The **LORD** said to me, “Proclaim all these words in Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s streets: Hear the words of this covenant and do them!
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to me, “Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, saying: ‘Hear the words of this covenant and do them.

verses.rationale: Renders early-rising idiom as repeated urgency rather than literal schedule.
verses.before: For I solemnly warned your ancestors from the day I brought them up from the land of Egypt until this day, rising early and warning them, saying, “Hear my voice.”
verses.after: From the day I brought your ancestors up from Egypt until today, I warned them insistently, again and again: ‘Listen to my voice.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For I solemnly warned your ancestors from the day I brought them up from the land of Egypt until this day, rising early and warning them, saying, “Hear my voice.”

verses.rationale: Keeps listening image and consequences as covenant terms, not an added curse list.
verses.before: But they did not hear or incline their ear. Each one walked in the stubbornness of their evil heart. So I brought upon them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to do, but they did not do.’”
verses.after: But they did not listen or incline their ears. Each followed the stubbornness of their evil heart. So I brought on them all the terms of this covenant, which I commanded them to carry out, but they did not.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But they did not hear or incline their ear. Each one walked in the stubbornness of their evil heart. So I brought upon them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to do, but they did not do.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves conspiracy charge and both locations.
verses.before: And the LORD said to me, “A conspiracy has been found among the people of Judah and among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.after: The **LORD** said to me, “A conspiracy has been found among the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to me, “A conspiracy has been found among the people of Judah and among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps return-to-sin contrast and names both houses.
verses.before: They have returned to the iniquities of their first ancestors, who refused to hear my words. They have gone after other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant that I made with their ancestors.
verses.after: They have returned to the sins of their forefathers, who refused to hear my words. They have followed other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have returned to the iniquities of their first ancestors, who refused to hear my words. They have gone after other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant that I made with their ancestors.

verses.rationale: Preserves troubling refusal of prayer without softening.
verses.before: So, thus says the LORD: “Look, I am bringing disaster upon them, from which they will not be able to escape. They will cry out to me, but I will not hear them.
verses.after: So this is what the **LORD** says: Look, I am bringing a disaster on them that they cannot escape. They will cry out to me, but I will not listen to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, thus says the LORD: “Look, I am bringing disaster upon them, from which they will not be able to escape. They will cry out to me, but I will not hear them.

verses.rationale: Makes divine referent clear and retains emphatic inability to save.
verses.before: Then the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to whom they burn incense, but they will not save them in the time of their disaster.
verses.after: Then Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s inhabitants will go and cry out to the gods to whom they burn offerings. But those gods will certainly not save them in their time of disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to whom they burn incense, but they will not save them in the time of their disaster.

verses.rationale: Preserves numerical comparison and derogatory Shame designation explained by Baal.
verses.before: For your gods have become as many as your cities, Judah; and as many as the streets of Jerusalem, you have set up altars to Shame—altars for burning incense to Baal.
verses.after: Judah, you have as many gods as cities. You have set up as many altars to Shame as there are streets in Jerusalem—altars for burning offerings to Baal.
verses.tsw_comparator: For your gods have become as many as your cities, Judah; and as many as the streets of Jerusalem, you have set up altars to Shame—altars for burning incense to Baal.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct prohibition to prophet and repeated prayer language.
verses.before: “But you, do not pray for this people. Do not lift up for them a cry or a prayer, for I will not hear when they call to me because of their disaster.
verses.after: As for you, do not pray for this people or lift up a cry or prayer for them. I will not listen when they call to me because of their disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But you, do not pray for this people. Do not lift up for them a cry or a prayer, for I will not hear when they call to me because of their disaster.

verses.rationale: Retains difficult pinned clause without silently replacing consonants; note records uncertainty.
verses.before: What is my beloved doing in my house, when she has carried out many schemes? Can holy flesh pass away from you? When you do evil, then you rejoice.
verses.after: What is my beloved doing in my house while so many carry out wicked schemes? Sacred meat will pass away from you; you rejoice in your evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: What is my beloved doing in my house, when she has carried out many schemes? Can holy flesh pass away from you? When you do evil, then you rejoice.

verses.rationale: Keeps named olive image and sudden destruction; avoids overidentifying the roar.
verses.before: A flourishing olive tree, beautiful with fine fruit— the LORD called your name. At the sound of a great tumult, he kindled fire upon it, and its branches were ruined.
verses.after: The **LORD** called you ‘A flourishing olive tree, beautiful with fine fruit.’ With the sound of a great roar, he set it on fire, and its branches were broken.
verses.tsw_comparator: A flourishing olive tree, beautiful with fine fruit— the LORD called your name. At the sound of a great tumult, he kindled fire upon it, and its branches were ruined.

verses.rationale: Preserves planter/judgment relation and third-to-first divine speech shift.
verses.before: The LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has spoken disaster against you because of the evil of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, which they have done to provoke me to anger by burning incense to Baal.
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts, who planted you, has pronounced disaster against you because of the evil the house of Israel and the house of Judah did, provoking me by burning offerings to Baal.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has spoken disaster against you because of the evil of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, which they have done to provoke me to anger by burning incense to Baal.

verses.rationale: Retains third-to-second person address and knowledge repetition.
verses.before: The LORD made it known to me, and I knew; then you showed me their deeds.
verses.after: The **LORD** made it known to me, and I knew. Then you showed me what they were doing.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD made it known to me, and I knew; then you showed me their deeds.

verses.rationale: Keeps innocent lamb and conspirators’ tree metaphor; fruit sense of food noted.
verses.before: Yet I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter, and I did not know that they had devised plans against me: “Let us destroy the tree with its bread; let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name will be remembered no more.”
verses.after: I was like a tame lamb led to slaughter. I did not know they were plotting against me: “Let’s destroy the tree with its fruit! Let’s cut him off from the land of the living, so his name is remembered no more.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter, and I did not know that they had devised plans against me: “Let us destroy the tree with its bread; let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name will be remembered no more.”

verses.rationale: Retains legal plea and vengeance; kidneys image explained in note.
verses.before: But, O LORD of Hosts, who judges righteously, who tests the inward parts and the heart, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have revealed my cause.
verses.after: But **LORD** of hosts, you judge justly and test the innermost being and heart. Let me see your vengeance on them, for I have laid my case before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But, O LORD of Hosts, who judges righteously, who tests the inward parts and the heart, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have revealed my cause.

verses.rationale: Keeps hometown threat, specific men, and both divine names.
verses.before: So, thus says the LORD concerning the people of Anathoth, who seek your life, saying, “Do not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or you will die by our hand”:
verses.after: So this is what the **LORD** says about the men of Anathoth who seek your life and say, “Do not prophesy in the **LORD**’s name, or you will die by our hands.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, thus says the LORD concerning the people of Anathoth, who seek your life, saying, “Do not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or you will die by our hand”:

verses.rationale: Retains age and gender distinctions and severe punishment.
verses.before: so, thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Look, I am about to punish them. Their young men will die by the sword; their sons and their daughters will die by famine.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** of hosts says: “Look, I am calling them to account. Their young men will die by the sword; their sons and daughters will die of hunger.
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore, thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Look, I am about to punish them. Their young men will die by the sword; their sons and their daughters will die by famine.

verses.rationale: Keeps no-remnant claim without harmonizing with later restoration.
verses.before: There will be no remnant for them, for I will bring disaster upon the people of Anathoth in the year of their punishment.”
verses.after: No remnant will remain for them, for I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth in the year they are called to account.”
verses.tsw_comparator: There will be no remnant for them, for I will bring disaster upon the people of Anathoth in the year of their punishment.”

verses.rationale: Keeps acknowledgment and genuine challenge together; no apologetic answer added.
verses.before: Righteous are you, LORD, when I bring a case against you; yet I would speak with you about matters of justice: Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why are everyone who deal treacherously at ease— people who deal in treachery?
verses.after: You are righteous, **LORD**, when I bring my case before you. Still, I want to speak with you about justice. Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why do all the treacherous live at ease?
verses.tsw_comparator: Righteous are you, LORD, when I bring a case against you; yet I would speak with you about matters of justice: Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why are all who deal treacherously at ease— those who deal in treachery?

verses.rationale: Retains divine responsibility in planting and mouth/inward contrast.
verses.before: You planted them; they have also taken root. They go on; they also bear fruit. You are near in their mouth, but far from their kidneys.
verses.after: You planted them, and they took root. They grow and bear fruit. You are near in their mouths but far from their innermost being.
verses.tsw_comparator: You planted them; they have also taken root. They go on; they also bear fruit. You are near in their mouth, but far from their kidneys.

verses.rationale: Preserves violent petition and consecration verb’s troubling use.
verses.before: But you, LORD, know me; you see me and test my heart toward you. Pull them away like sheep for slaughter; set them apart for a day of killing.
verses.after: But you, **LORD**, know me; you see me and test my heart toward you. Drag them away like sheep for slaughter; set them apart for the day of killing.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, LORD, know me; you see me and test my heart toward you. Pull them away like sheep for slaughter; set them apart for a day of killing.

verses.rationale: Retains ecological harm and ambiguous he; note gives uncertainty.
verses.before: How long will the land mourn and all the vegetation of the field wither? Because of the evil of people who live in it, livestock and birds are swept away, for they say, “He will not see our end.”
verses.after: How long will the land mourn and the grass in every field wither? Because of the evil of those who live there, animals and birds are swept away. For they say, ‘He will not see what happens to us.’
verses.tsw_comparator: How long will the land mourn and all the vegetation of the field wither? Because of the evil of those who live in it, livestock and birds are swept away, for they say, “He will not see our end.”

verses.rationale: Keeps demanding answer in paired images and notes pride/thicket idiom.
verses.before: If you have run with foot soldiers and they have wearied you, how will you compete with horses? And in a land of peace you are secure— but what will you do in the swelling of the Jordan?
verses.after: “If racing against people on foot has worn you out, how will you compete with horses? If you feel secure in a peaceful land, how will you manage in the Jordan’s thickets?
verses.tsw_comparator: If you have run with foot soldiers and they have wearied you, how will you compete with horses? And in a land of peace you are secure— but what will you do in the swelling of the Jordan?

verses.rationale: Retains family betrayal and loud cry without adding an unattested mob.
verses.before: For even your brothers and your father’s house— even they have dealt treacherously with you; even they have called after you at full voice. Do not trust them when they speak good things to you.
verses.after: Even your brothers and your father’s household have betrayed you. Even they shout after you at full voice. Do not trust them, even when they speak kindly to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For even your brothers and your father’s house— even they have dealt treacherously with you; even they have called after you at full voice. Do not trust them when they speak good things to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine loss, feminine beloved, and inheritance language.
verses.before: I have forsaken my house; I have abandoned my inheritance. I have given the beloved of my soul into the hand of her enemies.
verses.after: I have left my house, abandoned my inheritance. I have handed the beloved of my soul over to her enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have forsaken my house; I have abandoned my inheritance. I have given the beloved of my soul into the hand of her enemies.

verses.rationale: Preserves painful hate language and gendered lion image.
verses.before: My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest; she has raised her voice against me; so I hate her.
verses.after: My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest. She has roared against me; that is why I hate her.
verses.tsw_comparator: My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest; she has raised her voice against me; therefore I hate her.

verses.rationale: Retains uncertain bird image and predatory summons; hyena alternative noted.
verses.before: Is my inheritance to me a speckled bird of prey, with birds of prey all around her? Go, gather all the wild animals; bring them to devour.
verses.after: Is my inheritance a speckled bird of prey, with birds of prey surrounding her? Go, gather all the wild animals; bring them to devour!
verses.tsw_comparator: Is my inheritance to me a speckled bird of prey, with birds of prey all around her? Go, gather all the wild animals; bring them to devour.

verses.rationale: Keeps shepherd/vineyard mixed imagery and repeated plot.
verses.before: Many shepherds have ruined my vineyard; they have trampled my portion. They have made my delightful portion a desolate wilderness.
verses.after: Many shepherds have ruined my vineyard; they have trampled my plot of land. They have made my cherished plot a desolate wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many shepherds have ruined my vineyard; they have trampled my portion. They have made my delightful portion a desolate wilderness.

verses.rationale: Keeps land as mourning subject and lack of human attention.
verses.before: He has made it a desolation; desolate, it mourns to me. All the land is made desolate, because no one takes it to heart.
verses.after: It has been made a wasteland; desolate, it mourns before me. The whole land lies waste, because no one takes it to heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: He has made it a desolation; desolate, it mourns to me. All the land is made desolate, because no one takes it to heart.

verses.rationale: Retains consuming sword and broad flesh expression.
verses.before: Upon every bare height in the wilderness destroyers have come, for the sword of the LORD devours from one end of the land to the other end of the land; there is no peace for any flesh.
verses.after: Destroyers have come over all the bare heights in the wilderness. The **LORD** has a sword that devours from one end of the land to the other. No flesh has peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Upon every bare height in the wilderness destroyers have come, for the sword of the LORD devours from one end of the land to the other end of the land; there is no peace for any flesh.

verses.rationale: Keeps frustrating harvest and source shift from they to you.
verses.before: They have sown wheat and harvested thorns. They have worn themselves out; they will gain nothing. Be ashamed of your yields because of the burning anger of the LORD.
verses.after: They sowed wheat but reaped thorns. They exhausted themselves but gained nothing. Be ashamed of your harvests because of the **LORD**’s burning anger.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They have sown wheat and harvested thorns. They have worn themselves out; they will gain nothing. Be ashamed of your yields because of the burning anger of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves God’s own neighbors designation and repeated uprooting of different groups.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD concerning all my evil neighbors who touch the inheritance that I caused my people Israel to inherit: See, I am uprooting them from upon their land, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says about all my evil neighbors who lay hands on the inheritance I gave my people Israel: “Look, I will uproot them from their soil, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD concerning all my evil neighbors who touch the inheritance that I caused my people Israel to inherit: See, I am uprooting them from upon their land, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.

verses.rationale: Keeps compassion and return extended to neighboring peoples, not only Judah.
verses.before: And after I uproot them, I will again have compassion on them, and I will restore each person to their inheritance and each person to their land.
verses.after: After I have uprooted them, I will again have compassion on them and bring each back to their own inheritance and their own land.
verses.tsw_comparator: And after I uproot them, I will again have compassion on them, and I will restore each one to their inheritance and each one to their land.

verses.rationale: Retains conditional inclusion and reversal of religious teaching.
verses.before: And if they truly learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, “As the LORD lives,” just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up among my people.
verses.after: If they truly learn my people’s ways and swear by my name, ‘As the **LORD** lives’—just as they taught my people to swear by Baal—they will be built up among my people.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if they truly learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, “As the LORD lives,” just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up in the midst of my people.

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional threat alongside prior promise without reconciliation.
verses.before: But if they will not listen, I will uproot that nation, uprooting and destroying it, declares the LORD.
verses.after: But if they do not listen, I will uproot that nation completely and destroy it,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if they will not listen, I will uproot that nation, uprooting and destroying it, declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Uses waistcloth for worn linen object and retains water prohibition.
verses.before: Thus the LORD said to me: “Go, buy yourself a linen belt, and put it around your waist. But do not put it in water.”
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** said to me: “Go and buy a linen waistcloth. Put it around your waist, but do not put it in water.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus the LORD said to me: “Go, buy yourself a linen belt, and put it around your waist. But do not put it in water.”

verses.rationale: Preserves straightforward obedient action and repeated object.
verses.before: So I bought the belt, according to the word of the LORD, and put it around my waist.
verses.after: So I bought the waistcloth as the **LORD** had said and put it around my waist.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I bought the belt, according to the word of the LORD, and put it around my waist.

verses.rationale: Retains sequence of renewed speech.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to me a second time:
verses.after: The **LORD**’s word came to me a second time:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to me a second time:

verses.rationale: Retains Hebrew place-name rather than silently deciding Euphrates or local site.
verses.before: “Take the belt that you bought, which is around your waist. Get up, go to Perath, and hide it there in a crevice of the rock.”
verses.after: “Take the waistcloth you bought, the one around your waist. Go at once to Perath and hide it there in a crevice in the rock.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take the belt that you bought, which is around your waist. Get up, go to Perath, and hide it there in a crevice of the rock.”

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated location and obedience.
verses.before: So I went and hid it at Perath, as the LORD had commanded me.
verses.after: I went and hid it at Perath, as the **LORD** had commanded me.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I went and hid it at Perath, as the LORD had commanded me.

verses.rationale: Preserves indefinite elapsed time and retrieval command.
verses.before: After many days, the LORD said to me, “Get up, go to Perath, and take from there the belt that I commanded you to hide there.”
verses.after: Many days later, the **LORD** said to me, “Go at once to Perath and get the waistcloth I told you to hide there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: After many days, the LORD said to me, “Get up, go to Perath, and take from there the belt that I commanded you to hide there.”

verses.rationale: Keeps excavation and emphatic uselessness without adding an explanation of decay.
verses.before: So I went to Perath and dug, and I took the belt from the place where I had hidden it. And look—the belt was ruined; it was good for nothing.
verses.after: I went to Perath, dug up the waistcloth, and took it from the place where I had hidden it. It was ruined—good for nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I went to Perath and dug, and I took the belt from the place where I had hidden it. And look—the belt was ruined; it was good for nothing.

verses.rationale: Retains interpretation introduced as divine speech.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.after: Then the **LORD**’s word came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to me:

verses.rationale: Keeps ruin as connection between sign and meaning.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: “In this way I will ruin the great pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.
verses.after: “This is what the **LORD** says: In the same way, I will ruin Judah’s pride and Jerusalem’s great pride.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: “In this way I will ruin the great pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retains refusal, pursuit, service/worship, and repeated uselessness.
verses.before: This evil people, who refuse to listen to my words, who walk in the stubbornness of their heart, and who go after other gods to serve them and bow down to them, will become like this belt, good for nothing.
verses.after: This evil people refuses to listen to my words. They follow their stubborn hearts and go after other gods to serve and worship them. They will be like this waistcloth, good for nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: This evil people, who refuse to listen to my words, who walk in the stubbornness of their heart, and who go after other gods to serve them and bow down to them, will become like this belt, good for nothing.

verses.rationale: Keeps physical closeness, specific man, both houses, and fourfold intended relation.
verses.before: For just as a belt clings to a person’s waist, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to me,” declares the LORD, “to be for me a people, a name, a praise, and a glory. But they would not listen.
verses.after: As a waistcloth clings to a man’s waist, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to me,” declares the **LORD**, “to be my people, my name, my praise, and my glory. But they would not listen.
verses.tsw_comparator: For just as a belt clings to a person’s waist, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to me,” declares the LORD, “to be for me a people, a name, a praise, and a glory. But they would not listen.

verses.rationale: Retains seemingly obvious saying and mocking reply before explanation.
verses.before: “You will say to them this word: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Every jar will be filled with wine. And when they say to you, ‘Do we not certainly know that every jar will be filled with wine?’
verses.after: “Tell them this: This is what the **LORD**, Israel’s God, says: Every jar will be filled with wine. They will answer, ‘Don’t we know that every jar will be filled with wine?’
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall say to them this word: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Every jar will be filled with wine. And when they say to you, ‘Do we not certainly know that every jar will be filled with wine?’

verses.rationale: Preserves all groups and drunkenness as divine filling.
verses.before: then say to them: Thus says the LORD: Look, I am filling all the inhabitants of this land with drunkenness—the kings who sit for David on his throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.after: Then tell them: This is what the **LORD** says: Look, I am filling everyone who lives in this land with drunkenness—the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and everyone who lives in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: then say to them: Thus says the LORD: Look, I am filling all the inhabitants of this land with drunkenness—the kings who sit for David on his throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps violent jar metaphor and threefold refusal of pity.
verses.before: I will smash them, each person against another, fathers and children together,” declares the LORD. “I will not spare; I will not pity; I will not have compassion, so as to keep from destroying them.”
verses.after: I will smash them against one another, fathers and sons together,” declares the **LORD**. “No pity, no mercy, no compassion will keep me from destroying them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will smash them, each one against another, fathers and children together,” declares the LORD. “I will not spare; I will not pity; I will not have compassion, so as to keep from destroying them.”

verses.rationale: Retains paired listening commands and pride connection.
verses.before: Listen and give ear; do not be proud, for the LORD has spoken.
verses.after: Listen and pay attention; do not be proud, for the **LORD** has spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen and give ear; do not be proud, for the LORD has spoken.

verses.rationale: Keeps temporal urgency, stumbling setting, and recorded final verbal connection.
verses.before: Give glory to the LORD your God before he brings darkness, before your feet stumble on mountains at twilight. You hope for light, but he will make it deep darkness; he will turn it into gloom.
verses.after: Give glory to the **LORD** your God before he brings darkness, before your feet stumble on the mountains at dusk. You hope for light, but he will turn it to deep darkness, make it thick gloom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give glory to the LORD your God before he brings darkness, before your feet stumble on mountains at twilight. You hope for light, but he will make it deep darkness; he will turn it into gloom.

verses.rationale: Preserves concealed grief and shepherd image without merging voice into a narrator.
verses.before: But if you will not listen, my whole being will weep in secret because of your pride; my eyes will weep bitterly and flow with tears, because the flock of the LORD has been taken captive.
verses.after: But if you will not listen, my soul will weep in secret because of your pride. My eyes will weep bitterly and stream with tears, for the **LORD**’s flock has been taken captive.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you will not listen, my whole being will weep in secret because of your pride; my eyes will weep bitterly and flow with tears, because the flock of the LORD has been taken captive.

verses.rationale: Retains queen mother’s royal standing and lowered seat/crown image.
verses.before: Say to the king and to the queen mother, “Humble yourselves; sit down, for your splendid crowns have come down from your heads.”
verses.after: Say to the king and the queen mother, “Take a low seat, for your glorious crown has fallen from your heads.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to the king and to the queen mother, “Humble yourselves; sit down, for your splendid crowns have come down from your heads.”

verses.rationale: Keeps geographic Negeb and emphatic totality.
verses.before: The cities of the Negeb are shut up, with no one to open them. Judah has gone into exile—all of it; it has gone into exile completely.
verses.after: The cities of the Negeb are shut, with no one to open them. All Judah has gone into exile, wholly carried away.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cities of the Negeb are shut up, with no one to open them. Judah has gone into exile—all of it; it has gone into exile completely.

verses.rationale: Preserves entrustment question; English you accommodates written/read number change.
verses.before: Lift up your eyes and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock entrusted to you, your splendid flock?
verses.after: Lift your eyes and see those coming from the north! Where is the flock entrusted to you, your glorious sheep?
verses.tsw_comparator: Lift up your eyes and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock entrusted to you, your splendid flock?

verses.rationale: Adopts appointment sense with ambiguous clause noted; retains childbirth pain.
verses.before: What will you say when he appoints over you those whom you yourself taught to be leaders over you? Will not pains seize you like those of a woman in labor?
verses.after: What will you say when he sets over you as rulers those you trained to be your close friends? Will pain not seize you like a woman in labor?
verses.tsw_comparator: What will you say when he appoints over you those whom you yourself taught to be leaders over you? Will not pains seize you like those of a woman in labor?

verses.rationale: Preserves sexual violence implied by exposed skirts and violated heels; note names literal image.
verses.before: And if you say in your heart, “Why have these things happened to me?”—because of the greatness of your iniquity your skirts have been uncovered, your heels violated.
verses.after: And if you ask yourself, ‘Why has this happened to me?’— it is because of your great guilt that your skirts have been stripped back and your body violated.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if you say in your heart, “Why have these things happened to me?”—because of the greatness of your iniquity your skirts have been uncovered, your heels violated.

verses.rationale: Keeps specific ethnic comparison and sarcastic impossibility without implying dark skin itself is evil.
verses.before: Can a Cushite change his skin, or a leopard its spots? Then you also could do good, you who are trained to do evil.
verses.after: Can a Cushite change his skin, or a leopard its spots? Then you too could do good, though you are trained in doing evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Can a Cushite change his skin, or a leopard its spots? Then you also could do good, you who are trained to do evil.

verses.rationale: Keeps scatter image and third-person them.
verses.before: I will scatter them like chaff swept away by the wind of the wilderness.
verses.after: “I will scatter them like straw blown by a wilderness wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will scatter them like chaff swept away by the wind of the wilderness.
