verses.rationale: Preserves measured allotment and forgotten God/false trust pair.
verses.before: This is your lot, the portion measured out to you from me,” declares the LORD, “because you have forgotten me and trusted in falsehood.
verses.after: This is your lot, the portion I have measured out for you,” declares the **LORD**, “because you forgot me and trusted in falsehood.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is your lot, the portion measured out to you from me,” declares the LORD, “because you have forgotten me and trusted in falsehood.

verses.rationale: Retains divine agency and exposure metaphor without euphemizing harm.
verses.before: I myself will also lift your skirts over your face, and your shame will be seen.
verses.after: I myself will strip your skirts up over your face, and your shame will be seen.
verses.tsw_comparator: I myself will also lift your skirts over your face, and your shame will be seen.

verses.rationale: Keeps animal/sexual imagery and unsettled concluding question.
verses.before: Your adulteries, your lustful neighings, your shameless prostitution—on the hills in the field I have seen your detestable things. Woe to you, Jerusalem! Will you not be made clean? How long yet?”
verses.after: Your adulteries, your lustful neighing, your shameless prostitution— on the hills, in the open country, I have seen your abominations. Woe to you, Jerusalem! How much longer before you are clean?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Your adulteries, your lustful neighings, your shameless prostitution—on the hills in the field I have seen your detestable things. Woe to you, Jerusalem! Will you not be made clean? How long yet?”

verses.rationale: Retains plural droughts and prophetic heading.
verses.before: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah concerning the droughts:
verses.after: The **LORD**’s word that came to Jeremiah concerning the droughts:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah concerning the droughts:

verses.rationale: Keeps personified gates and downward/upward contrast.
verses.before: Judah mourns, and her gates languish; they sit in darkness on the ground, and the cry of Jerusalem rises.
verses.after: Judah mourns; her gates languish. They sink to the ground in mourning, and Jerusalem’s cry rises.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah mourns, and her gates languish; they sit in darkness on the ground, and the cry of Jerusalem rises.

verses.rationale: Renders lesser/younger ones as servants in context; retains mourning gesture.
verses.before: Her nobles send their servants for water; they come to the cisterns and find no water. They return with their vessels empty; they are ashamed and humiliated; they cover their heads.
verses.after: Her nobles send their servants for water. They come to the cisterns and find none. They return with empty jars, ashamed and humiliated, their heads covered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her nobles send their servants for water; they come to the cisterns and find no water. They return with their vessels empty; they are ashamed and humiliated; they cover their heads.

verses.rationale: Keeps cause of agricultural collapse and repeated gesture.
verses.before: Because the ground is dismayed, for there has been no rain in the land, the farmers are ashamed; they cover their heads.
verses.after: The ground is cracked, for no rain has fallen on the land. The farmers are ashamed; they cover their heads.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because the ground is dismayed, for there has been no rain in the land, the farmers are ashamed; they cover their heads.

verses.rationale: Retains animal suffering and reason without moralizing the mother.
verses.before: Even the doe in the field gives birth and abandons her young, because there is no grass.
verses.after: Even a doe in the field gives birth and abandons her fawn, because there is no grass.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even the doe in the field gives birth and abandons her young, because there is no grass.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact animal comparison and failing eyes.
verses.before: The wild donkeys stand on the bare heights; they pant for air like jackals. Their eyes fail, because there is no vegetation.
verses.after: Wild donkeys stand on the bare heights, panting for air like jackals. Their eyes fail because there is no vegetation.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wild donkeys stand on the bare heights; they pant for air like jackals. Their eyes fail, because there is no vegetation.

verses.rationale: Keeps confession as basis of plea and recurring turn language.
verses.before: Though our iniquities testify against us, LORD, act for the sake of your name. For our turnings away are many; we have sinned against you.
verses.after: Though our wrongs testify against us, **LORD**, act for your name’s sake. Our acts of turning away are many; we have sinned against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though our iniquities testify against us, LORD, act for the sake of your name. For our turnings away are many; we have sinned against you.

verses.rationale: Preserves challenging temporary-resident comparison and divine titles.
verses.before: Hope of Israel, its savior in a time of distress, why should you be like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who turns aside to spend the night?
verses.after: Hope of Israel, its savior in time of trouble, why are you like a resident foreigner in the land, a traveler who turns aside for the night?
verses.tsw_comparator: Hope of Israel, its savior in a time of distress, why should you be like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who turns aside to spend the night?

verses.rationale: Retains accusation of apparent helplessness alongside claim of belonging.
verses.before: Why should you be like one stunned, like a warrior unable to save? Yet you are among us, LORD, and your name is called over us. Do not leave us.
verses.after: Why are you like a stunned man, a warrior unable to save? Yet you are among us, **LORD**; your name is called over us. Do not abandon us!
verses.tsw_comparator: Why should you be like one stunned, like a warrior unable to save? Yet you are among us, LORD, and your name is called over us. Do not leave us.

verses.rationale: Keeps wandering feet and first-to-third-person divine statement.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD concerning this people: They have so loved to wander; they have not restrained their feet. Therefore the LORD does not accept them. Now he will remember their iniquity and call their sins to account.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says about this people: “They love to wander like this; they have not restrained their feet. So the **LORD** does not accept them. Now he will remember their guilt and call their sins to account.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD concerning this people: They have so loved to wander; they have not restrained their feet. Therefore the LORD does not accept them. Now he will remember their iniquity and call their sins to account.

verses.rationale: Keeps refusal of intercession concise and unsmoothed.
verses.before: And the LORD said to me, “Do not pray for the good of this people.
verses.after: The **LORD** said to me, “Do not pray for this people’s good.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to me, “Do not pray for the good of this people.

verses.rationale: Retains forms of worship and threefold destruction.
verses.before: Though they fast, I will not listen to their cry; though they offer burnt offering and grain offering, I will not accept them. Rather, by sword, famine, and plague I will bring them to an end.”
verses.after: When they fast, I will not hear their cry. When they offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. Instead, I will bring them to an end by sword, famine, and plague.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Though they fast, I will not listen to their cry; though they offer burnt offering and grain offering, I will not accept them. Rather, by sword, famine, and plague I will bring them to an end.”

verses.rationale: Keeps prophet’s objection and quoted divine claim within false prophecy.
verses.before: Then I said, “Ah, Lord GOD! Look—the prophets are telling them, ‘You will not see the sword, and famine will not come upon you; for I will give you true peace in this place.’”
verses.after: I said, “Ah, Lord **GOD**! The prophets keep telling them, ‘You will not see the sword, and famine will not come upon you. I will give you lasting peace in this place.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said, “Ah, Lord GOD! Look—the prophets are telling them, ‘You will not see the sword, and famine will not come upon you; for I will give you true peace in this place.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves three negated authorizations and fourfold false content; follows recorded deceit reading.
verses.before: And the LORD said to me, “The prophets are prophesying lies in my name. I have not sent them, commanded them, or spoken to them. They are prophesying to you a lying vision, divination, emptiness, and the deceit of their own hearts.
verses.after: The **LORD** said to me, “Those prophets are prophesying lies in my name. I did not send them, command them, or speak to them. What they prophesy to you is a lying vision, divination, emptiness, and the deceit of their own hearts.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to me, “The prophets are prophesying lies in my name. I have not sent them, commanded them, or spoken to them. They are prophesying to you a lying vision, divination, emptiness, and the deceit of their own hearts.

verses.rationale: Retains symmetrical denial and fate rather than compressing repetition.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD concerning the prophets who prophesy in my name, though I have not sent them, and who say, ‘Sword and famine will not come upon this land’: By sword and famine those prophets will come to their end.
verses.after: So this is what the **LORD** says about the prophets who prophesy in my name though I did not send them, who say, ‘Sword and famine will not come to this land’: By sword and famine those prophets will meet their end.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the prophets who prophesy in my name, though I have not sent them, and who say, ‘Sword and famine will not come upon this land’: By sword and famine those prophets will come to their end.

verses.rationale: Keeps full family victims and evil poured back upon perpetrators.
verses.before: And the people to whom they prophesy will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem because of the famine and the sword, with no one to bury them—them, their wives, their sons, and their daughters. I will pour out upon them their own evil.”
verses.after: The people to whom they prophesy will be thrown out in Jerusalem’s streets because of famine and sword. No one will bury them—them, their wives, their sons, or their daughters. I will pour their own evil upon them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the people to whom they prophesy will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem because of the famine and the sword, with no one to bury them—them, their wives, their sons, and their daughters. I will pour out upon them their own evil.”

verses.rationale: Retains personification, virgin designation, and repeated wound language.
verses.before: Say this word to them: Let my eyes run down with tears night and day, and let them not cease, for the virgin daughter of my people has been shattered with a great shattering, with a very grievous wound.
verses.after: Tell them this: ‘Let my eyes stream with tears night and day, without stopping. For my virgin daughter, my people, is broken with a great fracture, a terribly severe wound.
verses.tsw_comparator: Say this word to them: Let my eyes run down with tears night and day, and let them not cease, for the virgin daughter of my people has been shattered with a great shattering, with a very grievous wound.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired scenes and uncertain final travel clause without assuming trade or exile as certain.
verses.before: If I go out into the field, there are those slain by the sword; if I enter the city, there are those made sick by famine. For prophet and priest alike wander through a land they do not know.
verses.after: If I go out into the field—look, those slain by the sword! If I enter the city—look, those sick with hunger! Prophet and priest alike wander into a land they do not know.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: If I go out into the field, there are those slain by the sword; if I enter the city, there are those made sick by famine. For prophet and priest alike wander through a land they do not know.

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult questions and repeats 8:15’s hope/terror wording.
verses.before: Have you utterly rejected Judah? Does your whole being loathe Zion? Why have you struck us, leaving no healing for us? We wait for peace, but there is no good; for a time of healing, but look—there is terror.
verses.after: Have you utterly rejected Judah? Does your soul loathe Zion? Why have you struck us so that there is no healing for us? We hoped for peace, but no good came; for a time of healing, but look—terror!
verses.tsw_comparator: Have you utterly rejected Judah? Does your whole being loathe Zion? Why have you struck us, leaving no healing for us? We wait for peace, but there is no good; for a time of healing, but look—there is terror.

verses.rationale: Keeps shared inherited and present confession without transferring all blame backward.
verses.before: We acknowledge our wickedness, LORD, the iniquity of our ancestors; for we have sinned against you.
verses.after: We acknowledge our wickedness, **LORD**, and the guilt of our ancestors; we have sinned against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: We acknowledge our wickedness, LORD, the iniquity of our ancestors; for we have sinned against you.

verses.rationale: Retains direct appeal that God not break covenant.
verses.before: Do not despise us, for the sake of your name; do not dishonor the throne of your glory. Remember; do not break your covenant with us.
verses.after: For your name’s sake, do not spurn us; do not dishonor your glorious throne. Remember; do not break your covenant with us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not despise us, for the sake of your name; do not dishonor the throne of your glory. Remember; do not break your covenant with us.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired weather questions and hope grounded in divine making.
verses.before: Are there any among the worthless idols of the nations who can bring rain? Or can the heavens give showers? Are you not the one, the LORD our God? We wait for you, for you have made all these things.
verses.after: Can the nations’ empty idols bring rain? Can the heavens give showers? Is it not you, **LORD** our God? We wait in hope for you, for you have made all these things.
verses.tsw_comparator: Are there any among the worthless idols of the nations who can bring rain? Or can the heavens give showers? Are you not the one, the LORD our God? We wait for you, for you have made all these things.

verses.rationale: Keeps named intercessors and divine rejection, rendering soul idiom as heart’s inclination.
verses.before: The LORD said to me: “Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my whole being would not turn toward this people. Send them away from before me; let them go out.
verses.after: The **LORD** said to me, “Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my heart would not turn toward this people. Send them out of my presence. Let them go!
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to me: “Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my whole being would not turn toward this people. Send them away from before me; let them go out.

verses.rationale: Preserves four destinies and repeated relentless formula.
verses.before: When they ask you, “Where are we to go?” you are to say to them, “Thus says the LORD: Those destined for death, to death; those destined for the sword, to the sword; those destined for famine, to famine; those destined for captivity, to captivity.”
verses.after: When they ask you, ‘Where shall we go?’ tell them: This is what the **LORD** says: Those destined for death, to death; those for the sword, to the sword; those for famine, to famine; those for captivity, to captivity.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they ask you, “Where are we to go?” you are to say to them, “Thus says the LORD: Those destined for death, to death; those destined for the sword, to the sword; those destined for famine, to famine; those destined for captivity, to captivity.”

verses.rationale: Keeps four agents and distinct actions; destroyers supplied to make kinds intelligible.
verses.before: “I will appoint over them four kinds,” declares the LORD: “the sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth to devour and to destroy.
verses.after: “I will appoint four kinds of destroyers over them,” declares the **LORD**: “the sword to kill, dogs to drag away, birds of the sky and animals of the earth to devour and destroy.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will appoint over them four kinds,” declares the LORD: “the sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth to devour and to destroy.

verses.rationale: Preserves names, relationship, location, and historical attribution without adding explanation.
verses.before: I will make them an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, for what he did in Jerusalem.
verses.after: I will make them an object of horror to all the earth’s kingdoms because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and what he did in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make them an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, for what he did in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retains three questions and relational loss.
verses.before: For who will have compassion on you, Jerusalem? Who will mourn for you? Who will turn aside to ask after your well-being?
verses.after: Who will pity you, Jerusalem? Who will grieve for you? Who will turn aside to ask how you are?
verses.tsw_comparator: For who will have compassion on you, Jerusalem? Who will mourn for you? Who will turn aside to ask after your well-being?

verses.rationale: Retains divine weariness and temporal movement rather than theological resolution.
verses.before: “You have forsaken me,” declares the LORD. “You keep going backward. So I have stretched out my hand against you and destroyed you; I am weary of relenting.
verses.after: You abandoned me,” declares the **LORD**. “You keep moving backward. So I stretched out my hand against you and destroyed you. I am weary of relenting.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You have forsaken me,” declares the LORD. “You keep going backward. So I have stretched out my hand against you and destroyed you; I am weary of relenting.

verses.rationale: Keeps agricultural tool, gates, bereavement, and failure to return.
verses.before: I have winnowed them with a winnowing fork at the gates of the land. I have bereaved; I have destroyed my people. They did not turn from their ways.
verses.after: I winnowed them with a winnowing fork at the gates of the land. I bereaved and destroyed my people; they did not turn from their ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have winnowed them with a winnowing fork at the gates of the land. I have bereaved; I have destroyed my people. They did not turn from their ways.

verses.rationale: Keeps vulnerable mother and surprising noon attack; obscure anguish word noted.
verses.before: Their widows have become more numerous before me than the sand of the seas. Against the mother of a young man I have brought a destroyer at noon; suddenly I have made anguish and terrors fall upon her.
verses.after: Their widows became more numerous before me than the sand of the seas. Against the mother of a young man I brought a destroyer at noon. Suddenly I brought anguish and terrors upon her.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their widows have become more numerous before me than the sand of the seas. Against the mother of a young man I have brought a destroyer at noon; suddenly I have made anguish and terrors fall upon her.

verses.rationale: Retains seven, dying/daylight image, and source shift to survivors.
verses.before: She who bore seven has languished; she has breathed out her life. Her sun has gone down while it was still day; she is ashamed and humiliated. And their remnant I will give to the sword before their enemies,” declares the LORD.
verses.after: The mother of seven languishes; she breathes out her life. Her sun sets while it is still day; she is ashamed and humiliated. I will hand their survivors over to the sword before their enemies,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: She who bore seven has languished; she has breathed out her life. Her sun has gone down while it was still day; she is ashamed and humiliated. And their remnant I will give to the sword before their enemies,” declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps birth lament and absence of financial causes for dispute.
verses.before: Woe is me, my mother, that you bore me, a man of strife and a man of contention to all the land! I have neither lent, nor have they lent to me; yet every one of them curses me.
verses.after: Woe to me, my mother, that you gave birth to me— a man of dispute and contention for the whole land! I have neither lent nor borrowed, yet everyone curses me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe is me, my mother, that you bore me, a man of strife and a man of contention to all the land! I have neither lent, nor have they lent to me; yet every one of them curses me.

verses.rationale: Uses recorded release reading; notes difficulty and alternative strengthening sense.
verses.before: The LORD said: “Surely I have set you free for good; surely I have made the enemy entreat you in a time of evil and in a time of distress.
verses.after: The **LORD** said, “Surely I will set you free for good. Surely I will make the enemy plead with you in a time of disaster and distress.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said: “Surely I have set you free for good; surely I have made the enemy entreat you in a time of evil and in a time of distress.

verses.rationale: Keeps compressed metal question without inventing its referent.
verses.before: Can iron break iron from the north, and bronze?
verses.after: Can iron break iron— iron from the north—or bronze?
verses.tsw_comparator: Can iron break iron from the north, and bronze?

verses.rationale: Keeps loss without price and comprehensive territorial sin.
verses.before: Your wealth and your treasuries I will give as plunder, without price, because of all your sins throughout all your borders.
verses.after: I will give your wealth and treasures as plunder, without payment, because of all your sins throughout your territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your wealth and your treasuries I will give as plunder, without price, because of all your sins throughout all your borders.

verses.rationale: Preserves pinned make-pass verb with supplied object; note distinguishes make-serve alternative.
verses.before: I will make you pass over to your enemies into a land you do not know, for a fire has been kindled in my anger; it will burn against you.
verses.after: I will take you away with your enemies into a land you do not know. For a fire has been kindled in my anger; it will burn against you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make you pass over to your enemies into a land you do not know, for a fire has been kindled in my anger; it will burn against you.

verses.rationale: Keeps appeal against excessive patience toward enemies, without deleting vengeance.
verses.before: You know, LORD; remember me and attend to me, and avenge me against my persecutors. Do not take me away because of your patience. Know that for your sake I bear reproach.
verses.after: You know, **LORD**. Remember me and attend to me; avenge me on my persecutors. Do not let your patience with them carry me away. Know that I bear disgrace for your sake.
verses.tsw_comparator: You know, LORD; remember me and attend to me, and avenge me against my persecutors. Do not take me away because of your patience. Know that for your sake I bear reproach.

verses.rationale: Retains eating image, plural-to-singular recorded word, and name-bearing.
verses.before: Your words were found, and I ate them; your word became for me joy and the delight of my heart, for your name has been called upon me, LORD, God of Hosts.
verses.after: Your words were found, and I ate them. Your word became my joy and my heart’s delight, for your name is called over me, **LORD**, God of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your words were found, and I ate them; your word became for me joy and the delight of my heart, for your name has been called upon me, LORD, God of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine hand as source of isolation and anger.
verses.before: I did not sit in the company of revelers and rejoice. Because of your hand I sat alone, for you filled me with indignation.
verses.after: I did not sit rejoicing in the company of revelers. Because of your hand, I sat alone, for you filled me with indignation.
verses.tsw_comparator: I did not sit in the company of revelers and rejoice. Because of your hand I sat alone, for you filled me with indignation.

verses.rationale: Keeps accusation against God and water image without devotional softening.
verses.before: Why has my pain become unending, and my wound grievous, refusing to be healed? Will you indeed be to me like a deceptive brook, like waters that are not reliable?
verses.after: Why is my pain unending, my wound incurable, refusing to heal? Will you really be to me like a deceptive stream, waters that cannot be trusted?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why has my pain become unending, and my wound grievous, refusing to be healed? Will you indeed be to me like a deceptive brook, like waters that are not reliable?

verses.rationale: Preserves return/restoration word family and mouth metaphor.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD: “If you return, I will restore you, and you will stand before me. If you bring out what is precious from what is worthless, you will be as my mouth. Let them turn to you, but you must not turn to them.
verses.after: So this is what the **LORD** says: “If you return, I will restore you, and you will stand before me. If you bring out what is precious from what is worthless, you will be like my mouth. Let them return to you; you must not return to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD: “If you return, I will restore you, and you will stand before me. If you bring out what is precious from what is worthless, you will be as my mouth. Let them turn to you, but you must not turn to them.

verses.rationale: Keeps fortification image and divine presence promise tied to conflict.
verses.before: I will make you to this people a fortified wall of bronze. They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you to save you and to deliver you,” declares the LORD.
verses.after: I will make you a fortified bronze wall against this people. They will fight you but will not overcome you, for I am with you to save and deliver you,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make you to this people a fortified wall of bronze. They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you to save you and to deliver you,” declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains deliver/redeem pair and hand/palm variation as hand/grip.
verses.before: “I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked, and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless.”
verses.after: “I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked and redeem you from the grip of the ruthless.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked, and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless.”

verses.rationale: Preserves direct prophetic speech formula.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
verses.after: The **LORD**’s word came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to me, saying:

verses.rationale: Retains specific marriage/childbearing prohibition to Jeremiah without universalizing it.
verses.before: You must not take a wife for yourself, nor have sons or daughters in this place.
verses.after: “Do not take a wife or have sons and daughters in this place.
verses.tsw_comparator: You must not take a wife for yourself, nor have sons or daughters in this place.

verses.rationale: Keeps all family roles and emphatic local scope.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, and concerning the mothers who bear them and the fathers who father them in this land:
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** says about the sons and daughters born here, the mothers who bear them, and the fathers who father them in this land:
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, and concerning the mothers who bear them and the fathers who father them in this land:

verses.rationale: Retains diseased death, deprivation of burial, and animal consumption.
verses.before: They will die deaths of disease. They will not be mourned or buried; they will become dung on the surface of the ground. They will perish by sword and famine, and their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and for the animals of the earth.
verses.after: They will die of deadly diseases. They will not be mourned or buried; they will lie like dung on the ground. Sword and famine will consume them, and their corpses will be food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will die deaths of disease. They will not be mourned or buried; they will become dung on the surface of the ground. They will perish by sword and famine, and their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and for the animals of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps three divine gifts withdrawn and both name occurrences.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: Do not enter a house of mourning; do not go to mourn or show sympathy for them. For I have taken away my peace from this people, declares the LORD—steadfast love and compassion.
verses.after: “For this is what the **LORD** says: Do not enter a house of mourning. Do not go to lament or show sympathy for them, for I have withdrawn my peace from this people,” declares the **LORD**, “my steadfast love and compassion.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: Do not enter a house of mourning; do not go to mourn or show sympathy for them. For I have taken away my peace from this people, declares the LORD—steadfast love and compassion.

verses.rationale: Preserves actual ancient mourning practices without endorsing or explaining them in text.
verses.before: Both great and small will die in this land. They will not be buried, and no one will mourn for them, cut themselves, or shave their head for them.
verses.after: Great and small alike will die in this land. They will not be buried or mourned. No one will cut themselves or shave their head for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Both great and small will die in this land. They will not be buried, and no one will mourn for them, cut themselves, or shave their head for them.

verses.rationale: Makes implied bread explicit and retains both parents and ritual cup.
verses.before: No one will break bread for them in mourning, to comfort them for the dead; no one will give them the cup of consolation to drink for their father or their mother.
verses.after: No one will break bread for a mourner to offer comfort over the dead. No one will offer the cup of consolation over the loss of a father or mother.
verses.tsw_comparator: No one will break bread for them in mourning, to comfort them for the dead; no one will give them the cup of consolation to drink for their father or their mother.

verses.rationale: Keeps prohibition of ordinary celebration alongside mourning.
verses.before: And do not enter a house of feasting to sit with them, to eat and to drink.
verses.after: Do not enter a house of feasting to sit with them and eat and drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: And do not enter a house of feasting to sit with them, to eat and to drink.

verses.rationale: Preserves imminent eyewitness timing and wedding pair.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, before your eyes and in your days, I am bringing to an end in this place the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride.
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** of hosts, Israel’s God, says: Before your eyes, in your own days, I will silence in this place the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bridegroom and bride.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, before your eyes and in your days, I am bringing to an end in this place the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride.

verses.rationale: Keeps three protests and repeated divine name.
verses.before: When you tell this people all these words, and they say to you, “Why has the LORD spoken against us all this great disaster? What is our iniquity? What is our sin that we have committed against the LORD our God?”
verses.after: “When you tell this people all these things, they will ask you, ‘Why has the **LORD** pronounced this great disaster against us? What is our guilt? What sin have we committed against the **LORD** our God?’
verses.tsw_comparator: When you tell this people all these words, and they say to you, “Why has the LORD spoken against us all this great disaster? What is our iniquity? What is our sin that we have committed against the LORD our God?”

verses.rationale: Retains abandonment repetition and three religious acts.
verses.before: then say to them, “Because your ancestors forsook me, declares the LORD, and went after other gods, served them, and bowed down to them. They forsook me and did not keep my instruction.
verses.after: Tell them: ‘Because your ancestors abandoned me,’ declares the **LORD**. ‘They followed other gods, served them, and bowed down to them. They abandoned me and did not keep my instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: then say to them, “Because your ancestors forsook me, declares the LORD, and went after other gods, served them, and bowed down to them. They forsook me and did not keep my instruction.

verses.rationale: Keeps present generation’s greater culpability, not only inherited guilt.
verses.before: But you have acted more wickedly than your ancestors. Look, each of you follows the stubbornness of your evil heart, refusing to listen to me.
verses.after: And you have done worse than your ancestors! Each of you follows the stubbornness of an evil heart instead of listening to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you have acted more wickedly than your ancestors. Look, each of you follows the stubbornness of your evil heart, refusing to listen to me.

verses.rationale: Retains enforced exile and harsh absence of divine favor.
verses.before: So I will hurl you from this land into a land that neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will serve other gods day and night, for I will give you no favor.”
verses.after: So I will hurl you from this land into a land neither you nor your ancestors knew. There you will serve other gods day and night, for I will show you no favor.’
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will hurl you from this land into a land that neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will serve other gods day and night, for I will give you no favor.”

verses.rationale: Keeps surprising turn and first half of changed oath.
verses.before: So, look, days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be said, “As the LORD lives, who brought up the people of Israel from the land of Egypt,”
verses.after: “Yet look, days are coming,” declares the **LORD**, “when people will no longer say, ‘As the **LORD** lives, who brought the Israelites up from Egypt,’
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, look, days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be said, “As the LORD lives, who brought up the people of Israel from the land of Egypt,”

verses.rationale: Preserves north and all lands plus first-person restoration promise.
verses.before: but, “As the LORD lives, who brought up the people of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where he had driven them.” For I will bring them back to their land, which I gave to their ancestors.
verses.after: but, ‘As the **LORD** lives, who brought the Israelites up from the northern land and from all the lands where he had driven them.’ I will bring them back to the soil I gave their ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: but, “As the LORD lives, who brought up the people of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where he had driven them.” For I will bring them back to their land, which I gave to their ancestors.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated fish/hunt images and thorough pursuit; does not impose later evangelistic use.
verses.before: Look, I am sending for many fishers, declares the LORD, and they will catch them. Afterward I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them from every mountain and every hill, and from the clefts of the rocks.
verses.after: “Look, I am sending for many fishers,” declares the **LORD**, “and they will fish for them. Afterward I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them from every mountain and hill and from the crevices in the rocks.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am sending for many fishers, declares the LORD, and they will catch them. Afterward I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them from every mountain and every hill, and from the clefts of the rocks.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated eyes and double denial of concealment.
verses.before: For my eyes are on all their ways; they are not hidden from before me, nor is their iniquity concealed from my eyes.
verses.after: My eyes are on all their ways. They are not hidden from me, and their guilt is not concealed from my eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: For my eyes are on all their ways; they are not hidden from before me, nor is their iniquity concealed from my eyes.

verses.rationale: Keeps first, double, and disturbing corpse designation for idols.
verses.before: First I will repay double for their iniquity and their sin, because they have defiled my land with the carcasses of their detestable things and filled my inheritance with their abominations.
verses.after: First I will repay their guilt and sin double, because they have defiled my land with the corpses of their detestable things and filled my inheritance with their abominations.”
verses.tsw_comparator: First I will repay double for their iniquity and their sin, because they have defiled my land with the carcasses of their detestable things and filled my inheritance with their abominations.

verses.rationale: Retains nations’ future confession and ancestral inheritance reversal.
verses.before: O LORD, my strength and my stronghold, my refuge in the day of distress, to you nations will come from the ends of the earth and say, “Surely our ancestors inherited only falsehood, emptiness, and things in which there is no benefit.”
verses.after: **LORD**, my strength and stronghold, my refuge in the day of trouble, to you nations will come from the ends of the earth and say, ‘Our ancestors inherited nothing but lies, empty things with no use in them.’
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, my strength and my stronghold, my refuge in the day of distress, to you nations will come from the ends of the earth and say, “Surely our ancestors inherited only falsehood, emptiness, and things in which there is no benefit.”

verses.rationale: Keeps rhetorical question and emphatic denial.
verses.before: Can a human make gods for himself? Yet they are not gods.
verses.after: Can people make gods for themselves? Such things are not gods!
verses.tsw_comparator: Can a human make gods for himself? Yet they are not gods.

verses.rationale: Preserves threefold know and hand image.
verses.before: So, look, this time I will make them know; I will make them know my hand and my might. Then they will know that my name is the LORD.
verses.after: “So look, this time I will make them know; I will make them know my hand and my might. Then they will know that my name is the **LORD**.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, look, this time I will make them know; I will make them know my hand and my might. Then they will know that my name is the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves inscription and source shift their/your; hard-point identification noted.
verses.before: Judah’s sin is written with an iron stylus, with a point of diamond; it is engraved on the tablet of their heart and on the horns of your altars.
verses.after: Judah’s sin is written with an iron pen, engraved with a hard stone point on the tablet of their heart and on the horns of your altars.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah’s sin is written with an iron stylus, with a point of diamond; it is engraved on the tablet of their heart and on the horns of your altars.

verses.rationale: Keeps children as remembering subjects; alternate comparison noted.
verses.before: As their children remember their altars and their Asherah poles, beside flourishing trees, on the high hills,
verses.after: Their children remember their altars and Asherah poles beside flourishing trees on the high hills.
verses.tsw_comparator: As their children remember their altars and their Asherah poles, beside flourishing trees, on the high hills,

verses.rationale: Retains abrupt mountain address rather than moving it into preceding verse.
verses.before: my mountain in the open country— your wealth, all your treasures, I will give for plunder; your high places, because of sin throughout all your territories.
verses.after: My mountain in the open country, I will give your wealth and all your treasures as plunder, your high places because of sin throughout your territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: my mountain in the open country— your wealth, all your treasures, I will give for plunder; your high places, because of sin throughout all your territories.

verses.rationale: Keeps release/inheritance and explicit serve verb distinct from 15:14.
verses.before: You will let go of your inheritance, which I gave you; and I will make you serve your enemies in a land you have not known. For you have kindled a fire in my anger; it will burn forever.
verses.after: Through your own doing, you will let go of the inheritance I gave you. I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know. For you have kindled a fire in my anger; it will burn forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will let go of your inheritance, which I gave you; and I will make you serve your enemies in a land you have not known. For you have kindled a fire in my anger; it will burn forever.

verses.rationale: Retains flesh/arm image and heart turning, not a blanket ban on relationships.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Cursed is the man who trusts in humanity, who makes flesh his strength, and whose heart turns away from the LORD.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “Cursed is the one who trusts in human beings, makes flesh an arm of strength, and turns their heart away from the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Cursed is the man who trusts in humanity, who makes flesh his strength, and whose heart turns away from the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves plant/geographic image and lack of inhabited support.
verses.before: He will be like a shrub in the wilderness; he will not see when good comes. He will live in parched places in the desert, in a salt land where no one lives.
verses.after: That person will be like a shrub in the Arabah, never seeing good when it comes, living in scorched wilderness places, a salt land where no one lives.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will be like a shrub in the wilderness; he will not see when good comes. He will live in parched places in the desert, in a salt land where no one lives.

verses.rationale: Retains two divine names and repeated trust notion.
verses.before: Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD.
verses.after: Blessed is the one who trusts in the **LORD**, whose confidence is the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD.

verses.rationale: Follows recorded see reading rather than written fear; note gives both.
verses.before: He will be like a tree planted beside waters, sending out its roots beside a stream. It does not fear when heat comes; its leaves remain green. In a year of drought it is not anxious, and it does not cease to bear fruit.
verses.after: That person will be like a tree planted by water, sending roots toward a stream. It does not notice when heat comes; its leaves stay green. In a year of drought it is not anxious and does not stop bearing fruit.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He will be like a tree planted beside waters, sending out its roots beside a stream. It does not fear when heat comes; its leaves remain green. In a year of drought it is not anxious, and it does not cease to bear fruit.

verses.rationale: Keeps severe heart diagnosis and question without substituting doctrinal label.
verses.before: The heart is more deceitful than anything, and desperately sick— who can understand it?
verses.after: The heart is more deceitful than anything, and desperately sick. Who can understand it?
verses.tsw_comparator: The heart is more deceitful than anything, and desperately sick— who can understand it?

verses.rationale: Retains heart/kidneys pairing and fruit metaphor; recorded plural ways.
verses.before: I, the LORD, search the heart; I test the inward parts, to give to each according to their way, according to the fruit of their deeds.
verses.after: “I, the **LORD**, search the heart and test the innermost being, to give each person according to their ways, according to the fruit of their deeds.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I, the LORD, search the heart; I test the inward parts, to give to each according to their way, according to the fruit of their deeds.

verses.rationale: Keeps ancient bird comparison without claiming modern zoological proof.
verses.before: Like a partridge that broods over eggs it did not lay is one who makes wealth unjustly. In the middle of their days it will leave them, and in their end they will prove to be a fool.
verses.after: Like a partridge that broods over eggs it did not lay is one who gains wealth unjustly. In the middle of life it will leave them; in the end they will prove a fool.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a partridge that broods over eggs it did not lay is one who makes wealth unjustly. In the middle of their days it will leave them, and in their end they will prove to be a fool.

verses.rationale: Preserves compact temple praise without inserting a divine name.
verses.before: A throne of glory, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.
verses.after: A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: A throne of glory, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Keeps recorded first-person me amid address, marks voice shift, and retains spring image.
verses.before: O Hope of Israel, LORD, everyone who forsake you will be put to shame. People who turn away from me will be written in the earth, for they have forsaken the fountain of living water, the LORD.
verses.after: **LORD**, hope of Israel, all who abandon you will be ashamed. “Those who turn away from me will be written in the dust,” for they have abandoned the **LORD**, the spring of living water.
verses.tsw_comparator: O Hope of Israel, LORD, all who forsake you will be put to shame. Those who turn away from me will be written in the earth, for they have forsaken the fountain of living water, the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves familiar paired prayer without forced novelty.
verses.before: Heal me, LORD, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for you are my praise.
verses.after: Heal me, **LORD**, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for you are my praise.
verses.tsw_comparator: Heal me, LORD, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for you are my praise.

verses.rationale: Keeps opponents’ challenge rather than treating it as sincere inquiry.
verses.before: Look, they are saying to me, “Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come now.”
verses.after: They keep saying to me, “Where is the **LORD**’s word? Let it come!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, they are saying to me, “Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come now.”

verses.rationale: Retains difficult shepherd clause with alternative noted; keeps denial of desiring disaster.
verses.before: Yet I have not hurried away from being a shepherd after you, nor have I desired the day of disaster. You know what came from my lips; it was before your face.
verses.after: But I have not rushed away from shepherding in your service, nor have I longed for the dreadful day. You know; what left my lips was before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I have not hurried away from being a shepherd after you, nor have I desired the day of disaster. You know what came from my lips; it was before your face.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct appeal that God not become feared harm.
verses.before: Do not become a terror to me; you are my refuge in the day of evil.
verses.after: Do not become a terror to me; you are my refuge in the day of disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not become a terror to me; you are my refuge in the day of evil.

verses.rationale: Preserves imprecation, contrasts, and double devastation.
verses.before: Let people who pursue me be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame. Let them be dismayed, but do not let me be dismayed. Bring upon them a day of evil; break them with a double breaking.
verses.after: Let my persecutors be ashamed, not me. Let them be terrified, not me. Bring the day of disaster on them; break them with a double breaking.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let those who pursue me be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame. Let them be dismayed, but do not let me be dismayed. Bring upon them a day of evil; break them with a double breaking.

verses.rationale: Keeps gate designation, royal movement, and expanded locations.
verses.before: Thus the LORD said to me: “Go and stand at the gate of the people, through which the kings of Judah enter and leave, and at all the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** said to me: “Go and stand at the People’s Gate, through which Judah’s kings enter and leave, and at all Jerusalem’s gates.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus the LORD said to me: “Go and stand at the gate of the people, through which the kings of Judah enter and leave, and at all the gates of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retains threefold audience and public setting.
verses.before: Say to them: ‘Hear the word of the LORD, kings of Judah, all Judah, and everyone who live in Jerusalem, who enter through these gates.
verses.after: Say to them: Hear the **LORD**’s word, kings of Judah, all Judah, and all Jerusalem’s inhabitants who enter through these gates.
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to them: ‘Hear the word of the LORD, kings of Judah, all Judah, and all who live in Jerusalem, who enter through these gates.

verses.rationale: Keeps life-stakes idiom and concrete carrying prohibition.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Take care for your own lives, and do not carry a load on the Sabbath day or bring it through the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: Take care for your lives. Do not carry a load on the Sabbath day or bring one through Jerusalem’s gates.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Take care for your own lives, and do not carry a load on the Sabbath day or bring it through the gates of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retains domestic and general work restrictions with holiness language.
verses.before: Do not bring a load out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do no work; but keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your ancestors.
verses.after: Do not take a load out of your houses on the Sabbath day or do any work. Keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not bring a load out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do no work; but keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your ancestors.

verses.rationale: Keeps both body idioms and refusal to receive discipline.
verses.before: But they did not listen or incline their ear. They stiffened their necks so as not to listen and not to receive instruction.
verses.after: But they did not listen or incline their ears. They stiffened their necks, refusing to listen or accept correction.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they did not listen or incline their ear. They stiffened their necks so as not to listen and not to receive instruction.

verses.rationale: Preserves extended condition and recorded masculine reference to day.
verses.before: “If you truly listen to me,” declares the LORD, “not bringing a load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, but keeping the Sabbath day holy and doing no work on it,
verses.after: “If you truly listen to me,” declares the **LORD**, “bringing no load through this city’s gates on the Sabbath day and keeping the Sabbath holy by doing no work on it,
verses.tsw_comparator: “If you truly listen to me,” declares the LORD, “not bringing a load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, but keeping the Sabbath day holy and doing no work on it,

verses.rationale: Retains pinned coordination and repeated officials rather than silently simplifying court list.
verses.before: then kings and officials, sitting on David’s throne, will enter through the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horses—they and their officials, the people of Judah, and people who live in Jerusalem. This city will be inhabited forever.
verses.after: then kings and officials sitting on David’s throne will enter this city’s gates, riding in chariots and on horses—they and their officials, the people of Judah and Jerusalem’s inhabitants. This city will be inhabited forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: then kings and officials, sitting on David’s throne, will enter through the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horses—they and their officials, the people of Judah, and those who live in Jerusalem. This city will be inhabited forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves six areas and distinct offerings; geography vocabulary supplied separately.
verses.before: People will come from the towns of Judah, from the places around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the lowland, from the hill country, and from the Negeb, bringing whole offerings, sacrifices, grain offerings, and frankincense, and bringing thank offerings to the house of the LORD.
verses.after: People will come from Judah’s cities and the country around Jerusalem, from Benjamin’s territory, the Shephelah, the hill country, and the Negeb. They will bring burnt offerings, sacrifices, grain offerings, and frankincense, and bring thank offerings into the **LORD**’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: People will come from the towns of Judah, from the places around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the lowland, from the hill country, and from the Negeb, bringing whole offerings, sacrifices, grain offerings, and frankincense, and bringing thank offerings to the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps negative condition, repetition, and unquenched fire threat.
verses.before: But if you do not listen to me, to keep the Sabbath day holy by not carrying a load and entering through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will kindle a fire in its gates. It will consume the palaces of Jerusalem, and it will not be quenched.”
verses.after: But if you do not listen to me by keeping the Sabbath day holy and not carrying loads through Jerusalem’s gates on the Sabbath day, I will kindle a fire in her gates. It will consume Jerusalem’s palaces and will not be put out.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you do not listen to me, to keep the Sabbath day holy by not carrying a load and entering through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will kindle a fire in its gates. It will consume the palaces of Jerusalem, and it will not be quenched.”

verses.rationale: Keeps prophetic introduction and named recipient.
verses.before: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying:
verses.after: The word that came to Jeremiah from the **LORD**:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying:

verses.rationale: Preserves physical descent and promised hearing.
verses.before: “Rise, go down to the potter’s house, and there I will let you hear my words.”
verses.after: “Go down to the potter’s house. There I will let you hear my words.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Rise, go down to the potter’s house, and there I will let you hear my words.”

verses.rationale: Renders two-stones tool as potter’s wheel and follows recorded demonstrative.
verses.before: So I went down to the potter’s house, and there he was, working at the wheel.
verses.after: I went down to the potter’s house. He was there, working at the wheel.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I went down to the potter’s house, and there he was, working at the wheel.

verses.rationale: Keeps remaking and potter’s judgment; does not state a cause of spoilage.
verses.before: But the vessel he was making from clay was spoiled in the potter’s hand, so he made it again into another vessel, as seemed right to the potter to make.
verses.after: The clay vessel he was making was spoiled in the potter’s hand. So he made it again into another vessel, as he thought best.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the vessel he was making from clay was spoiled in the potter’s hand, so he made it again into another vessel, as seemed right to the potter to make.

verses.rationale: Retains interpretation’s separate speech event.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.after: Then the **LORD**’s word came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to me:

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated house of Israel and hand comparison.
verses.before: “Can I not do with you as this potter has done, house of Israel?” declares the LORD. “Look: as clay is in the potter’s hand, so you are in my hand, house of Israel.
verses.after: “House of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter does?” declares the **LORD**. “Like clay in the potter’s hand, so you are in my hand, house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Can I not do with you as this potter has done, house of Israel?” declares the LORD. “Look: as clay is in the potter’s hand, so you are in my hand, house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps three destructive commission verbs and general nation scope.
verses.before: At one moment I may speak concerning a nation or a kingdom, to uproot, to tear down, and to destroy it;
verses.after: At one moment I may speak about a nation or kingdom, to uproot, tear down, and destroy it.
verses.tsw_comparator: At one moment I may speak concerning a nation or a kingdom, to uproot, to tear down, and to destroy it;

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit conditional divine relenting without theological harmonization.
verses.before: but if that nation turns from its evil, concerning which I have spoken, I will relent of the disaster that I planned to bring upon it.
verses.after: But if that nation turns from the evil I spoke against, I will relent from the disaster I planned to bring on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: but if that nation turns from its evil, concerning which I have spoken, I will relent of the disaster that I planned to bring upon it.

verses.rationale: Keeps constructive pair and parallel scenario.
verses.before: At another moment I may speak concerning a nation or a kingdom, to build and to plant it;
verses.after: At another moment I may speak about a nation or kingdom, to build and plant it.
verses.tsw_comparator: At another moment I may speak concerning a nation or a kingdom, to build and to plant it;

verses.rationale: Preserves symmetrical withdrawal of good and recorded evil reading.
verses.before: but if it does what is evil in my sight, not listening to my voice, I will relent of the good that I said I would do for it.
verses.after: But if it does what is evil in my eyes and does not listen to my voice, I will relent from the good I said I would do for it.
verses.tsw_comparator: but if it does what is evil in my sight, not listening to my voice, I will relent of the good that I said I would do for it.

verses.rationale: Keeps shaping link to potter and urgent individual return within collective address.
verses.before: “Now say, please, to the people of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Thus says the LORD: Look, I am shaping disaster against you and devising a plan against you. Turn back, each of you, from your evil way, and make your ways and your deeds good.”
verses.after: “Now tell the people of Judah and Jerusalem’s inhabitants: This is what the **LORD** says: Look, I am shaping disaster against you and devising a plan against you. Turn, each of you, from your evil way, and put your ways and deeds right.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Now say, please, to the people of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Thus says the LORD: Look, I am shaping disaster against you and devising a plan against you. Turn back, each of you, from your evil way, and make your ways and your deeds good.”

verses.rationale: Preserves brazen quoted refusal and own-plans contrast.
verses.before: But they will say, “It is hopeless! For we will follow our own plans, and each of us will act according to the stubbornness of an evil heart.”
verses.after: But they say, ‘It’s no use! We will follow our own plans. Each of us will act on the stubbornness of our evil heart.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: But they will say, “It is hopeless! For we will follow our own plans, and each of us will act according to the stubbornness of an evil heart.”

verses.rationale: Retains virgin personification and appeal to international witness.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD: “Ask among the nations: who has heard such things? The virgin Israel has done a most horrible thing.
verses.after: So this is what the **LORD** says: “Ask among the nations: who has heard anything like this? Virgin Israel has done a most horrifying thing.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD: “Ask among the nations: who has heard such things? The virgin Israel has done a most horrible thing.

verses.rationale: Keeps snow and water questions with uncertain rocky-country/foreign-water wording noted.
verses.before: Does the snow of Lebanon leave the rock of the open field? Or are cold, flowing waters, foreign waters, plucked away?
verses.after: Does Lebanon’s snow leave the rocky heights? Do waters from far away stop flowing, cold and running?
verses.tsw_comparator: Does the snow of Lebanon leave the rock of the open field? Or are cold, flowing waters, foreign waters, plucked away?

verses.rationale: Retains forgotten God, emptiness, and contrast of established and unmade roads.
verses.before: Yet my people have forgotten me; they burn incense to a worthless thing. They have made them stumble in their ways, the ancient paths, to walk on bypaths, on a road not built up,
verses.after: Yet my people have forgotten me; they burn offerings to emptiness. They have been made to stumble in their ways, the ancient paths, to walk on bypaths, a road not built up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet my people have forgotten me; they burn incense to a worthless thing. They have made them stumble in their ways, the ancient paths, to walk on bypaths, on a road not built up,

verses.rationale: Keeps physical gestures of derision rather than generic disapproval.
verses.before: making their land a horror, an object of perpetual hissing. Everyone who passes by it will be appalled and shake their head.
verses.after: They make their land a horror, an object of endless hissing. Everyone who passes will be appalled and shake their head.
verses.tsw_comparator: making their land a horror, an object of perpetual hissing. Everyone who passes by it will be appalled and shake their head.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine bodily image and reversal of relational presence.
verses.before: Like an east wind I will scatter them before the enemy. I will show them my back, not my face, in the day of their disaster.”
verses.after: Like an east wind, I will scatter them before the enemy. I will show them my back, not my face, on the day of their calamity.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Like an east wind I will scatter them before the enemy. I will show them my back, not my face, in the day of their disaster.”

verses.rationale: Keeps institutional confidence, three roles, and verbal assault idiom.
verses.before: Then they said, “Come, let us devise plans against Jeremiah, for instruction will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor word from the prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and let us not listen to any of his words.”
verses.after: Then they said, “Come, let’s devise plans against Jeremiah. Instruction will not disappear from the priest, counsel from the wise, or a word from the prophet. Come, let’s strike him with the tongue and pay no attention to anything he says.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they said, “Come, let us devise plans against Jeremiah, for instruction will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor word from the prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and let us not listen to any of his words.”

verses.rationale: Keeps contrast with opponents’ refusal to listen.
verses.before: Listen to me, LORD, and hear the voice of people who contend with me.
verses.after: Pay attention to me, **LORD**; listen to what my opponents are saying.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen to me, LORD, and hear the voice of those who contend with me.

verses.rationale: Retains former intercession as ground for protest.
verses.before: Should evil be repaid for good? Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak good on their behalf, to turn your wrath away from them.
verses.after: Should evil repay good? They have dug a pit for my life! Remember how I stood before you to speak good on their behalf, to turn your fury away from them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Should evil be repaid for good? Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak good on their behalf, to turn your wrath away from them.

verses.rationale: Keeps entire harsh imprecation and distinct family victims without blessing or censoring it.
verses.before: So give their children to famine; hand them over to the power of the sword. Let their wives become bereaved and widowed; let their men be slain by death, their young men struck down by the sword in battle.
verses.after: So give their children over to famine; pour them out to the power of the sword. Let their wives be childless widows; let their men be struck down by death, their young men by the sword in battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore give their children to famine; hand them over to the power of the sword. Let their wives become bereaved and widowed; let their men be slain by death, their young men struck down by the sword in battle.

verses.rationale: Preserves corresponding trap/raid imagery and recorded pit reading.
verses.before: Let a cry be heard from their houses when you suddenly bring a raiding band upon them; for they have dug a pit to capture me and have hidden traps for my feet.
verses.after: Let a cry be heard from their houses when you suddenly bring raiders against them. For they dug a pit to catch me and hid snares for my feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let a cry be heard from their houses when you suddenly bring a raiding band upon them; for they have dug a pit to capture me and have hidden traps for my feet.

verses.rationale: Retains negative forgiveness petition and divine anger appeal as prophet’s speech.
verses.before: But you, LORD, know all their plans against me for death. Do not cover over their guilt or blot out their sin from before you. Let them be made to stumble before you; in the time of your anger, act against them.
verses.after: But you, **LORD**, know all their plans to kill me. Do not forgive their guilt or blot out their sin from before you. Let them be brought down before you; deal with them in the time of your anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, LORD, know all their plans against me for death. Do not cover over their guilt or blot out their sin from before you. Let them be made to stumble before you; in the time of your anger, act against them.

verses.rationale: Supplies take implied by following with-group; preserves two sets of elders.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Go, buy a potter’s earthenware flask. Take some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests,
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** said: “Go and buy an earthenware jar from a potter. Take some of the elders of the people and some of the senior priests,
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Go, buy a potter’s earthenware flask. Take some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests,

verses.rationale: Retains valley and recorded gate name, with location uncertainty noted.
verses.before: and go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, at the entrance of the Potsherd Gate. There proclaim the words that I will speak to you.
verses.after: and go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, at the entrance of the Potsherd Gate. There proclaim the words I tell you.
verses.tsw_comparator: and go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, at the entrance of the Potsherd Gate. There proclaim the words that I will speak to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps both divine names and startling ears image.
verses.before: Say: Hear the word of the LORD, kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am bringing such disaster on this place that the ears of everyone who hears of it will ring.
verses.after: Say: Hear the **LORD**’s word, kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. This is what the **LORD** of hosts, Israel’s God, says: Look, I am bringing disaster on this place that will make the ears of everyone who hears it ring.
verses.tsw_comparator: Say: Hear the word of the LORD, kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am bringing such disaster on this place that the ears of everyone who hears of it will ring.

verses.rationale: Preserves estrangement and actual bloodshed, not only false worship.
verses.before: Because they have forsaken me and made this place foreign, and have burned incense in it to other gods whom neither they nor their ancestors nor the kings of Judah have known, and because they have filled this place with innocent blood.
verses.after: They have abandoned me and made this place foreign. Here they have burned offerings to other gods, gods neither they nor their ancestors nor Judah’s kings knew. They have filled this place with innocent blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because they have forsaken me and made this place foreign, and have burned incense in it to other gods whom neither they nor their ancestors nor the kings of Judah have known, and because they have filled this place with innocent blood.

verses.rationale: Keeps specific sons and triple divine disavowal.
verses.before: They have built the high places of Baal to burn their children in the fire as whole offerings to Baal—something I did not command, did not speak of, and that never entered my heart.
verses.after: They have built Baal’s high places to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal—something I never commanded, never spoke of, and that never entered my mind.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have built the high places of Baal to burn their children in the fire as whole offerings to Baal—something I did not command, did not speak of, and that never entered my heart.

verses.rationale: Matches earlier valley naming and retains transformation of place-name.
verses.before: So, look, days are coming, declares the LORD, when this place will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.
verses.after: So look, days are coming,” declares the **LORD**, “when this place will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, look, days are coming, declares the LORD, when this place will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

verses.rationale: Retains emptying wordplay with jar and physical death consequences.
verses.before: I will empty out the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem in this place. I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies and by the hand of those seeking their lives. I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth.
verses.after: I will empty out Judah’s and Jerusalem’s plans in this place. I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies, by the hands of those seeking their lives. I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will empty out the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem in this place. I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies and by the hand of those seeking their lives. I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated hissing and city wounds image.
verses.before: I will make this city a horror and an object of hissing. Everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will hiss because of all its wounds.
verses.after: I will make this city a horror and an object of hissing. Everyone who passes will be appalled and hiss at all its wounds.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make this city a horror and an object of hissing. Everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will hiss because of all its wounds.

verses.rationale: Keeps cannibalism, divine agency, and siege pressure fully explicit.
verses.before: I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters; each person will eat the flesh of a neighbor in the siege and distress with which their enemies and those seeking their lives will press them.
verses.after: I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and daughters. They will eat one another’s flesh in the siege and distress their enemies, those seeking their lives, inflict on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters; each one will eat the flesh of a neighbor in the siege and distress with which their enemies and those seeking their lives will press them.

verses.rationale: Preserves witnessed sign-act and specific male witnesses.
verses.before: Then break the flask before the eyes of the people who go with you,
verses.after: “Then break the jar in front of the men who went with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then break the flask before the eyes of the people who go with you,

verses.rationale: Keeps irreparable baked vessel distinct from remoldable clay and burial-space cause.
verses.before: and say to them: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: In this way I will break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter’s vessel that cannot be repaired again. They will bury in Topheth because there is no place left to bury.
verses.after: Tell them: This is what the **LORD** of hosts says: In the same way, I will break this people and this city, as someone breaks a potter’s vessel that can never be repaired. People will bury the dead at Topheth for lack of room to bury them elsewhere.
verses.tsw_comparator: and say to them: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: In this way I will break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter’s vessel that cannot be repaired again. They will bury in Topheth because there is no place left to bury.

verses.rationale: Preserves extension of valley judgment to city.
verses.before: Thus I will do to this place, declares the LORD, and to its inhabitants, making this city like Topheth.
verses.after: This is what I will do to this place and its inhabitants,” declares the **LORD**. “I will make this city like Topheth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus I will do to this place, declares the LORD, and to its inhabitants, making this city like Topheth.

verses.rationale: Keeps roof worship and two offering types, without modernizing celestial host.
verses.before: The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will become unclean like the place of Topheth—all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to all the host of the heavens and poured out drink offerings to other gods.
verses.after: Jerusalem’s houses and the houses of Judah’s kings will be unclean like Topheth—all those houses whose roofs were used to burn offerings to all the host of heaven and pour drink offerings to other gods.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will become unclean like the place of Topheth—all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to all the host of the heavens and poured out drink offerings to other gods.

verses.rationale: Keeps movement from valley to temple and both names.
verses.before: Then Jeremiah came from Topheth, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy. He stood in the court of the house of the LORD and said to all the people,
verses.after: Jeremiah returned from Topheth, where the **LORD** had sent him to prophesy. He stood in the courtyard of the **LORD**’s house and said to all the people,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jeremiah came from Topheth, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy. He stood in the court of the house of the LORD and said to all the people,

verses.rationale: Preserves satellite towns, comprehensive warning, and stiff-neck idiom.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am bringing on this city and on all its towns all the disaster that I have spoken against it, because they stiffened their neck so as not to listen to my words.
verses.after: “This is what the **LORD** of hosts, Israel’s God, says: Look, I am bringing on this city and all its towns every disaster I pronounced against it, because they stiffened their necks and would not listen to my words.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am bringing on this city and on all its towns all the disaster that I have spoken against it, because they stiffened their neck so as not to listen to my words.

verses.rationale: Makes office and family relationship clear without conflating later namesakes.
verses.before: Now Pashhur son of Immer, the priest, who was chief officer in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.
verses.after: Pashhur son of Immer, the priest who was chief officer in the **LORD**’s house, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Pashhur son of Immer, the priest, who was chief officer in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.

verses.rationale: Retains physical abuse, restraint, and precise temple gate.
verses.before: Then Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks that were in the upper Benjamin Gate of the house of the LORD.
