verses.after: Pashhur beat Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks at the Upper Benjamin Gate in the **LORD**’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks that were in the upper Benjamin Gate of the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Translates new name for audible connection to following terror refrain.
verses.before: The next day, when Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks, Jeremiah said to him, “The LORD does not call your name Pashhur, but Terror on Every Side.
verses.after: The next day, when Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks, Jeremiah told him, “The name the **LORD** gives you is Terror on Every Side, not Pashhur.
verses.tsw_comparator: The next day, when Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks, Jeremiah said to him, “The LORD does not call your name Pashhur, but Terror on Every Side.

verses.rationale: Preserves terror assignment, witnessed deaths, and Babylon’s explicit arrival.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: Look, I am making you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. They will fall by the sword of their enemies while your eyes look on. And I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon; he will carry them away into exile in Babylon and strike them down with the sword.
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** says: Look, I am making you a terror to yourself and all your friends. They will fall by their enemies’ sword while you watch. I will hand all Judah over to the king of Babylon, who will carry them into exile in Babylon and strike them with the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: Behold, I am making you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. They shall fall by the sword of their enemies while your eyes look on. And I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon; he shall carry them away into exile in Babylon and strike them down with the sword.

verses.rationale: Retains accumulating all phrases and three stages of removal.
verses.before: I will give all the wealth of this city, all its gains, all its precious things, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah into the hand of their enemies, who will plunder them and seize them and carry them to Babylon.
verses.after: All this city’s wealth, all it has earned, all its precious things, and all the treasures of Judah’s kings—I will hand them over to their enemies. They will plunder them, seize them, and take them to Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will give all the wealth of this city, all its gains, all its precious things, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah into the hand of their enemies, who shall plunder them and seize them and carry them to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated there and connects friends’ fate to false prophecy.
verses.before: And you, Pashhur, and everyone who dwell in your house will go into captivity. To Babylon you will go, and there you will die, and there you will be buried—you and all your friends to whom you have prophesied falsely.”
verses.after: And you, Pashhur, and everyone in your household will go into captivity. You will go to Babylon, die there, and be buried there—you and all the friends to whom you prophesied lies.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, Pashhur, and all who dwell in your house shall go into captivity. To Babylon you shall go, and there you shall die, and there you shall be buried—you and all your friends to whom you have prophesied falsely.”

verses.rationale: Keeps accusation and force; note allows persuaded/enticed without neutralizing protest.
verses.before: You enticed me, O LORD, and I was enticed; you overpowered me and prevailed. I have become a laughingstock all the day; everyone mocks me.
verses.after: You deceived me, **LORD**, and I was deceived. You overpowered me and prevailed. I have become a laughingstock all day long; everyone mocks me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You enticed me, O LORD, and I was enticed; you overpowered me and prevailed. I have become a laughingstock all the day; everyone mocks me.

verses.rationale: Keeps compelled message and repeated all-day suffering.
verses.before: For whenever I speak, I cry out; I proclaim, “Violence and destruction!” For the word of the LORD has become for me a reproach and derision all the day.
verses.after: Whenever I speak, I cry out; I shout, “Violence! Destruction!” The **LORD**’s word has brought me reproach and ridicule all day long.
verses.tsw_comparator: For whenever I speak, I cry out; I proclaim, “Violence and destruction!” For the word of the LORD has become for me a reproach and derision all the day.

verses.rationale: Preserves attempted silence and embodied inescapable fire without inspirational additions.
verses.before: If I say, “I will not mention him or speak any more in his name,” then there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones; I am weary of holding it in, and I cannot.
verses.after: I said, “I will not mention him or speak in his name anymore.” But then it was like a burning fire in my heart, shut up in my bones. I grew weary of holding it in; I could not.
verses.tsw_comparator: If I say, “I will not mention him or speak any more in his name,” then there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones; I am weary of holding it in, and I cannot.

verses.rationale: Keeps friends’ betrayal and deceived/prevail echoes of verse 7.
verses.before: For I hear the whispering of many: “Terror on every side! Denounce him! Let us denounce him!” All my close friends watch for my stumbling: “Perhaps he will be enticed, and we can prevail against him and take our revenge on him.”
verses.after: I hear many whispering, “Terror on every side! Denounce him! Let’s denounce him!” All my close friends watch for me to stumble: “Perhaps he can be deceived. Then we can prevail over him and take our revenge.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I hear the whispering of many: “Terror on every side! Denounce him! Let us denounce him!” All my close friends watch for my stumbling: “Perhaps he will be enticed, and we can prevail against him and take our revenge on him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves confidence, warrior image, and third prevail occurrence.
verses.before: But the LORD is with me like a mighty warrior; so my persecutors will stumble, and they will not prevail. They will be greatly put to shame, for they will not succeed; their everlasting disgrace will not be forgotten.
verses.after: But the **LORD** is with me like a fearsome warrior. So my persecutors will stumble and not prevail. They will be deeply ashamed because they have not succeeded, with an everlasting humiliation that will not be forgotten.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD is with me like a mighty warrior; therefore my persecutors will stumble, and they will not prevail. They will be greatly put to shame, for they will not succeed; their everlasting disgrace will not be forgotten.

verses.rationale: Retains righteous as tested object and repeated legal vengeance plea from 11:20.
verses.before: O LORD of Hosts, who tests the righteous, who sees the kidneys and the heart, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have committed my cause.
verses.after: **LORD** of hosts, you test the righteous and see the innermost being and heart. Let me see your vengeance on them, for I have laid my case before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD of Hosts, who tests the righteous, who sees the kidneys and the heart, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have committed my cause.

verses.rationale: Keeps both names and abrupt praise before renewed lament.
verses.before: Sing to the LORD; praise the LORD! For he has delivered the life of the needy from the hand of evildoers.
verses.after: Sing to the **LORD**; praise the **LORD**! For he has delivered the life of the needy from the hand of evildoers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing to the LORD; praise the LORD! For he has delivered the life of the needy from the hand of evildoers.

verses.rationale: Preserves reversal from praise to birth curse without editorial transition.
verses.before: Cursed be the day on which I was born! Let the day when my mother bore me not be blessed!
verses.after: Cursed be the day I was born! Let the day my mother bore me never be blessed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cursed be the day on which I was born! Let the day when my mother bore me not be blessed!

verses.rationale: Keeps male-child announcement and messenger curse.
verses.before: Cursed be the man who brought the news to my father, saying, “A son is born to you,” making him very glad.
verses.after: Cursed be the man who brought my father the news, “A son, a boy, has been born to you!” and filled him with joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cursed be the man who brought the news to my father, saying, “A son is born to you,” making him very glad.

verses.rationale: Retains unnamed cities and two times of terror.
verses.before: Let that man be like the cities that the LORD overthrew without pity; let him hear a cry in the morning and an alarm at noon,
verses.after: Let that man be like the cities the **LORD** overthrew without relenting. Let him hear a cry in the morning and an alarm at noon,
verses.tsw_comparator: Let that man be like the cities that the LORD overthrew without pity; let him hear a cry in the morning and an alarm at noon,

verses.rationale: Preserves disturbing unrealized death wish and womb/grave paradox.
verses.before: because he did not kill me in the womb, so that my mother would have been my grave, and her womb forever pregnant.
verses.after: because he did not kill me in the womb, so my mother would have been my grave and her womb pregnant forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: because he did not kill me in the womb, so that my mother would have been my grave, and her womb forever pregnant.

verses.rationale: Leaves chapter’s final despair unanswered, as in the source.
verses.before: Why did I come out from the womb to see toil and sorrow, and spend my days in shame?
verses.after: Why did I come out of the womb to see toil and sorrow and spend my days in shame?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why did I come out from the womb to see toil and sorrow, and spend my days in shame?

comparative_references.scope: All 287 TSW verses read after independent drafting from each selected Hebrew record and all annotations. Shared wording retained where clear; overlap is triage only.
